summary: The [minister's one-or-two-national-backup-centres position stands](2025-05-27-leconomie-cenadi-datacenter-study), with no instrument, site or appropriation behind it since May 2025.
developments:
2025-05 - a study was restituted and the minister [stated a policy of concentrating state resources on one or two national backup centres rather than multiplying public facilities](2025-05-27-leconomie-cenadi-datacenter-study), the study [framed as a step to digital independence](2025-05-26-cenadi-digital-independence-data-centres-itweb).

The position has not moved since. No instrument, site or appropriation is on record, and the 269-page study that surveyed thirteen administrations is not itself held, so which facilities would be consolidated and on what timetable is unknown.

summary: The [state operator was tasked with carrying national data and infrastructure interoperability on 18 August 2026](2026-08-18-dba-fgi-cameroun-camtel-interoperabilite-nationale), with no design or timetable published.
developments:
2026-08-18 - the posts and telecommunications ministry [tasked the state operator with carrying national data and infrastructure interoperability, the mandate given at the opening of the national internet governance forum and resting on the operator's backbone, transmission, access and hosting infrastructure](2026-08-18-dba-fgi-cameroun-camtel-interoperabilite-nationale).

No design, timetable, budget or instrument is published. An interoperability mandate handed to a commercial operator rather than established in law leaves unstated which bodies are obliged to connect, on what standard, and who arbitrates a refusal.

progress: Stalled, recommendations delivered and no strategy adopted
summary: A [February 2026 workshop delivered recommendations for an AI framework that is still absent](2026-02-18-digitalbusiness-recommandations-ia-cameroun-strategie-nationale).
developments:
[A ministerial workshop on 17 and 18 February 2026 delivered recommendations to the minister calling for a progressive risk-based AI regulatory framework, an interministerial coordination mechanism and a dedicated observatory or authority, all of them still absent](2026-02-18-digitalbusiness-recommandations-ia-cameroun-strategie-nationale). [UNESCO published a national report on AI ethics with the ministry in February 2026](2026-02-13-unesco-rapport-national-ethique-ia-minpostel), and [a regulatory sandbox for artificial intelligence had been announced in June 2024](2024-06-19-minpostel-intelligence-artificielle-sandbox-reglementaire).

Recommendations are not regulation. No national AI strategy, coordination mechanism or authority exists on the record.

summary: Operators [secure over 73% of the country's domains domestically against a national target of 98% by 2026](2025-12-11-camtel-unveils-performance-of-its-zamengoe-datacenter).
developments:
2025-12-10 to 12 - the state operator stated that [operators including itself secure over 73% of the country's domains domestically against a national target of 98% by 2026, and put revenue from its data-transport activities above FCFA 33.7bn in 2024, more than 17% up on 2023](2025-12-11-camtel-unveils-performance-of-its-zamengoe-datacenter).

The figures are the operator's own. No localisation instrument, obligation or exemption regime sits behind the target, no independent measurement of it has been published by the regulator or the agency, and nothing states what happens if it is missed.

summary: The [2026 internet governance forum put data at the foundation of interoperable infrastructure](2026-08-19-237online-cameroon-internet-governance-forum) with no national framework on record for it to build on.
developments:
2026-08-18 to 20 - the forum was [held at Yaounde on the theme of moving from fragmentation to interoperability, positioning data as the foundation for interoperable digital public infrastructure](2026-08-19-237online-cameroon-internet-governance-forum), [trailed the week before](2026-08-12-cameroon-fgi-2026-data-governance-preview).

No national data-governance framework exists on the record for the theme to rest on, and no programme document, participant list or outcome text is held, so what was resolved is unrecorded. The interoperability the theme names has no instrument behind it beyond a mandate given to the state operator at the same event.

summary: A national open-data policy is [provided for in the artificial-intelligence roadmap and nothing has been published](2025-07-08-snia-2040-ai-roadmap-seven-pillars-techafricanews).
developments:
The policy was [provided for in the 2040 roadmap presented in July 2025, with nothing published](2025-07-08-snia-2040-ai-roadmap-seven-pillars-techafricanews), and the position is the same at both ends of the window.

It is [not among the ten priority areas tabled to cabinet on 30 July 2026](2026-07-31-cameroon-pm-national-ai-strategy-completion), which is the nearest thing to a status update the base holds: the instrument that would carry it has been reordered around other things. No draft, consultation or publication schedule exists on record.

summary: [Loi n. 2024/017 on personal data protection is in force and unamended](2024-12-23-cmr-loi-2024-017-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel), with no supervisory authority operating.
developments:
The law was [promulgated on 23 December 2024 and is in force, with no supervisory authority operating](2024-12-23-cmr-loi-2024-017-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel), a position [restated to the National Assembly in April 2025](2025-04-08-leconomie-minpostel-minister-national-assembly-digital-inclusion).

Nothing in the window amended it. The promulgated text was acquired in July 2026 and is held as a 24-page page-image scan of which pages 15 to 24 are unread, so what the statute obliges beyond its first half is not established from anything on file.

summary: [Loi n. 2010/012 remains in force and is invoked to justify network restrictions](2026-06-16-lejour-cybercrime-laws-threaten-freedoms); no reform is adopted on record.
developments:
The law has stood since 21 December 2010 and is [in force and invoked to justify network restrictions, with civil-society reform recommendations pending and none adopted on record](2026-06-16-lejour-cybercrime-laws-threaten-freedoms).

The recommendations were addressed to government after a workshop in June 2026. Nothing since reports a government response, a drafting instruction or a bill. The statute is the legal basis under which the restrictions recorded elsewhere in this report were imposed, which is why its non-reform is the material fact rather than its age.

summary: [Decret n. 2025/059 on identity titles](2025-02-28-cameroun-decret-2025-059-titres-identitaires) and the [2024 civil-registration law](2025-01-27-new-civil-registration-law-sdg-16-9-biometricupdate) are both in force and unamended.
developments:
The decree was [signed on 28 February 2025 governing five identity-title classes and is in force, unamended](2025-02-28-cameroun-decret-2025-059-titres-identitaires); its refugee and disability chapters are not captured in the base.

The [civil-registration law was enacted on 23 December 2024 in 130 sections, providing for electronic declaration, a national database, digital certificates and a unique personal identification number](2025-01-27-new-civil-registration-law-sdg-16-9-biometricupdate), and is also unamended. Its text is not held, so what the unique personal identification number obliges, and how it relates to the biometric card, is not checkable from anything on file.

progress: No change, a standing statute the base holds for the first time
summary: [Loi 2010/021 on electronic commerce has been in force since December 2010](2010-12-21-loi-2010-021-commerce-electronique-cameroun), with its [implementing decree from 2011](2011-06-15-cameroun-decret-2011-1521-commerce-electronique-modalites).
developments:
[Loi 2010/021 on electronic commerce was enacted on 21 December 2010](2010-12-21-loi-2010-021-commerce-electronique-cameroun), [Decret 2011-1521 fixed its modalities in June 2011](2011-06-15-cameroun-decret-2011-1521-commerce-electronique-modalites), and [Decret 2012-1318 constituted the electronic certification authority under it](2012-05-22-decret-2012-1318-autorite-certification-electronique).

The statutory chain is complete and nothing on the file reports enforcement, a certified provider count or a transaction volume under it.

progress: No change, a standing statute the base holds for the first time
summary: [Loi 2020/010 on statistical activity has been in force since July 2020](2020-07-20-loi-2020-010-activite-statistique-cameroun), with its [2021 implementing decree](2021-12-02-cameroun-decret-2021-690-activite-statistique-modalites).
developments:
[Loi 2020/010 on statistical activity was enacted on 20 July 2020](2020-07-20-loi-2020-010-activite-statistique-cameroun) and [Decret 2021-690 fixed its modalities in December 2021](2021-12-02-cameroun-decret-2021-690-activite-statistique-modalites). [The statistics institute has published guidelines for producing statistics from administrative sources under it](2022-10-14-ins-manuel-lignes-directrices-statistiques-source-administrative).

No compliance report or statistical council record under the statute is held.

summary: The [e-government and access to information bill is still a preliminary draft](2023-05-22-avant-projet-loi-acces-information-publique-transformation-numerique-administration); the [2018 transparency code stands](2026-04-16-leconomie-citizen-budget-oversight-east).
developments:
The bill is [a preliminary draft on the right of access to and use of public information and the digital transformation of the administration, circulated in May 2023](2023-05-22-avant-projet-loi-acces-information-publique-transformation-numerique-administration). Later reporting on its progress is in the base but is not citable, so the position stated here is older than the record.

The [transparency and good governance code promulgated on 11 July 2018 remains in force, requiring budget-information dissemination and civil-society involvement, and the finance ministry was still running first-contact sensitisation with civil society in April 2026](2026-04-16-leconomie-citizen-budget-oversight-east) - eight years after promulgation.

summary: The authority is [created in law, not established and unfunded](2024-12-23-cmr-loi-2024-017-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel), with [no appropriation in the FY2025 or FY2026 estimates](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-45-451).
developments:
The authority was [created by the December 2024 statute as an independent public body, so the function does not sit with the existing information technology agency](2024-12-23-cmr-loi-2024-017-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel), and it is not established.

[No appropriation for it appears in the FY2025 or FY2026 estimates](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-45-451); the statute's only appearance in a finance law is a tax derogation from it. Nothing in the window named a president, a seat, a staff or a commencement decree, so a data-protection law has been in force for the whole window with nobody empowered to apply it.

summary: Personal-data systems multiplied with no supervisor: a [private address register entered the identity stack](2025-06-19-cameroons-findme-rides-new-bank-deal-scale-digital-addressing) and a [driver-monitoring system was presented with no regime published](2026-05-02-mtn-cameroon-ai-road-safety-camtrack-techreviewafrica).
developments:
2025-06-19 - a bank partnership [required every new customer to supply a geolocated postal address certified through a startup's postal-operator tie-up, reaching more than 700,000 clients of that bank, at FCFA 2,000 a certification](2025-06-19-cameroons-findme-rides-new-bank-deal-scale-digital-addressing) - a privately run register entering the identity-verification stack without a legislative act.

2026-05 - a [driver-behaviour monitoring system was presented and awarded at the first national road-safety forum, with no deployment scale, contract, fleet count or data-protection regime published](2026-05-02-mtn-cameroon-ai-road-safety-camtrack-techreviewafrica).

Both process personal data in volume in a year in which the authority that would supervise them was not established.

summary: A regional expert panel [recommended terrestrial gateways inside the region's jurisdiction and citizens' data stored on the continent](2026-02-24-trb-artac-10th-ordinary-session-kinshasa-ngso-techreviewafrica).
developments:
2026-02-24 - at the regional regulators' tenth ordinary session an expert panel [recommended a satellite data-residency framework: terrestrial gateways inside the region's jurisdiction, operator-equivalent financial obligations, and citizens' data stored on the continent](2026-02-24-trb-artac-10th-ordinary-session-kinshasa-ngso-techreviewafrica).

It is a panel recommendation, not an adopted regional instrument, and no member state has since enacted any part of it on the record. Cameroon's own satellite position - a licence file undecided for two years and a standing seizure circular - sits alongside it without either being reconciled to the other.

The central bank adopted a regional financial inclusion strategy for 2025-2029 covering the six member states, validated by the monetary union's ministerial committee on 21 December 2023 and published in February 2025 ([strategy](2025-02-01-beac-strategie-regionale-inclusion-financiere-cemac)); the base holds no member-state implementation plan, target or outturn under it.

summary: An [interoperable QR-code standard was launched under a regional regulation of 8 April 2026](2026-07-30-cemac-gimac-norme-qr-code-interoperable), binding across the six member states.
developments:
2026-07-29 - the standard was [launched at Douala under a regional regulation of 8 April 2026, so that any bank, microfinance or mobile-money application can scan any merchant code across the six member states, routed and settled through the regional switch](2026-07-30-cemac-gimac-norme-qr-code-interoperable), [validated by the regional ministerial committee in April 2026](2026-07-30-gabonreview-beac-qr-code-interoperable-cemac).

It is a regional instrument binding on Cameroonian institutions rather than a national one. No national transposition, compliance deadline or supervisory finding is on file, and no count of Cameroonian merchants or applications on the standard has been published.

summary: The [Chad border fibre memorandum was suspended on sovereignty grounds](2026-02-09-chad-fast-track-ndjamena-mbere-fiber-link-cameroon-connectingafrica) and [regional free roaming missed its June 2026 deadline](2026-02-24-trb-artac-10th-ordinary-session-kinshasa-ngso-techreviewafrica).
developments:
A [cooperation agreement of May 2025 promised the Chad border section within fourteen days](2025-05-16-cameroon-chad-digital-cooperation-agreement-techreviewafrica). It is [not built: the April 2025 memorandum was suspended by Chad's regulator on digital-sovereignty grounds and the parties told to revise and re-sign](2026-02-09-chad-fast-track-ndjamena-mbere-fiber-link-cameroon-connectingafrica). Cameroon is Chad's only submarine-cable entry point, so the suspension is a regional connectivity fact rather than a bilateral one.

A [resolution mandating effective free roaming by 30 June 2026 passed its deadline with no record of implementation](2026-02-24-trb-artac-10th-ordinary-session-kinshasa-ngso-techreviewafrica); Cameroon's regulator was in the adopting delegation.

summary: Central African states [met in Douala to draft a regional framework on cross-border data flows](2026-09-03-7joursinfo-eccas-cross-border-data-governance-workshop), agreeing its pillars rather than its text.
developments:
Experts from Central African member states met in this country's second city from 31 August to 4 September 2026 to assess national readiness and agree the pillars of a regional framework governing cross-border data flows, with technical and financial support from the German development agency, a continental development agency, the Economic Commission for Africa and the African Union Commission ([workshop](2026-09-03-7joursinfo-eccas-cross-border-data-governance-workshop)).

Pillars only: no draft text, adoption route, timetable or stated relationship to the continental data policy framework is published, and the base holds no national position on cross-border transfer against which to read the regional work.

summary: [Quality-of-service monitoring platforms were handed to the regulator in January 2026](2026-01-07-trb-receives-qos-monitoring-platforms-patnuc-techafricanews), replacing manual inspection.
developments:
At the window's opening the regulator issued [sanctions off manual inspections, fining two operators in July 2025](2025-07-11-art-fines-orange-mtn-4-6-million-telecomreviewafrica), with no dedicated monitoring platform on record.

2026-01-07 - [platforms were handed over by the national connectivity project and the World Bank](2026-01-07-trb-receives-qos-monitoring-platforms-patnuc-techafricanews), and [field inspections of three operators followed at Douala on 13 and 14 April 2026](2026-04-16-art-field-inspections-qos-coverage-douala-techafricanews).

No sanction is on record since the platforms were handed over, and no measurement out of them has been published, so whether the new capability has changed either enforcement or the reported quality is unestablished.

2026-08-13 - a finance ministry order [reclassified the regulator from the third to the second category of public establishments, set on its average realised budget across the 2022, 2023 and 2024 financial years](2026-08-17-art-cameroun-2e-categorie-etablissements-publics), affecting its institutional standing and pay structure; the order text and the budget figures behind it are not published.

summary: The regional switch [renewed its PCI DSS v4.0.1 certification in March 2026](2026-04-10-gimac-renouvelle-certification-pci-dss-v4-0-1), and [device certification guidelines were issued](2025-11-10-trb-device-certification-guidelines-digital-safety-techafricanews).
developments:
2026-03 - the sub-region's electronic-transaction processor [renewed its PCI DSS v4.0.1 certification for the infrastructure on which it processes and transmits bank-card data, the certificate issued by an external assessor](2026-04-10-gimac-renouvelle-certification-pci-dss-v4-0-1). It is a regional body's certification, carried here because the national switch traffic runs through it.

2025-11-10 - the regulator [issued certification guidelines for devices sold in Cameroon under its digital-safety campaign](2025-11-10-trb-device-certification-guidelines-digital-safety-techafricanews), which precede the import-duty regime that followed in April 2026. No conformity register, test regime or enforcement finding has been published against either.

summary: The [2026 internet governance forum convened at Yaounde](2026-08-19-237online-cameroon-internet-governance-forum), and the finance ministry [began civil-society budget sensitisation](2026-04-16-leconomie-citizen-budget-oversight-east).
developments:
2026-08-18 to 20 - the [national internet governance forum was held at Yaounde](2026-08-19-237online-cameroon-internet-governance-forum), the first edition the base records; no prior edition, participant list or outcome text is held, so what non-governmental participants contributed is unrecorded.

2026-04 - the finance ministry was [running first-contact sensitisation with civil society on budget oversight, eight years after the transparency code that requires civil-society involvement was promulgated](2026-04-16-leconomie-citizen-budget-oversight-east).

The pattern in both is a channel opening without an output: a forum with no resolutions on file and a consultation obligation reaching first contact after eight years.

summary: [Four shutdowns were recorded in 2025, including election-period restrictions on social platforms](2026-03-01 Rising Repression Meets Global Resistance Internet Shutdowns in 2025), against none the year before.
developments:
The base recorded no restriction in the year to August 2025.

2025-10-23 - restrictions were imposed during the presidential poll, part of [four shutdowns recorded in Cameroon in 2025, including election-period restrictions on social platforms](2026-03-01 Rising Repression Meets Global Resistance Internet Shutdowns in 2025). One of the four was a cross-border cut that took the Central African Republic off a submarine cable.

The legal basis is the [2010 cybercrime law, in force and invoked to justify network restrictions, with civil-society reform recommendations pending and none adopted](2026-06-16-lejour-cybercrime-laws-threaten-freedoms). No order, duration or authorising instrument for any of the four has been published.

progress: Mixed, the sector programme was tabled 71.5% up while the cadastre line was cut 44.2% and the universal-service fund stays abolished
summary: The [telecommunications ministry's merged programme was tabled at FCFA 19,494,457,000 for FY2026](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-45-451), while the [cadastre line was cut 44.2%](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-37-380).
developments:
The FY2026 finance bill [merges the development and cybersecurity programmes into one at FCFA 19,494,457,000, a 71.5% increase on the FY2025 combined appropriation](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-45-451) of [FCFA 10,330,875,000 plus FCFA 1,037,044,000](2024-12-23-cmr-2025-45-130). It is proposed stage only: the enacted law is a page-image scan the base cannot read.

The lands ministry's cadastre programme went the other way, [FCFA 874,046,000 proposed for FY2026 against FCFA 1,567,500,000 appropriated for FY2025](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-37-380), a 44.2% cut and below the [FY2024 level](2023-12-19-cmr-2024-37-026).

The [Special Telecommunications Development Fund, a special account funded by 3% of operators' turnover plus half the regulator's year-end surplus, stays abolished, and universal-service money is not separately traceable in FY2024, FY2025 or FY2026](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-45-451).

summary: A [three-year master service agreement with Ethio Telecom was signed on 5 December 2025](2025-12-05-ethio-telecom-camtel-master-service-agreement-telecomreviewafrica) across four workstreams.
developments:
2025-12-05 - the state operator [signed a three-year framework covering fintech support, architecture and deployment of a sovereign government cloud, network expansion consultancy and institutional digital culture](2025-12-05-ethio-telecom-camtel-master-service-agreement-telecomreviewafrica), the visiting team [concluding its work later that month](2025-12-16-ethio-telecom-team-concludes-strategic-visit-camtel-telecomreviewafrica).

No fee, investment or cost-sharing figure attaches to the agreement, and no delivery is reported against the sovereign government cloud workstream - which is the workstream that would matter most, given that the state's own cloud policy has not moved since May 2025.

summary: A [syndicated FCFA 44.884bn network financing was signed in January 2026](2026-01-22-camtel-cbc-44-884bn-fcfa-mobile-network-expansion-techafricanews), while a [US$225m operator pledge stayed an announcement](2025-01-01-mtn-cameroon-cmr-2025-network-capex-pledge-bw03).
developments:
Financial technology and foreign-exchange rules, rather than the investment case, dominated a business climate forum in Yaoundé ([report](2026-08-27-cmr-businessincameroon-regulatory-hurdles-us-investment)), and an assessment named what still deters United States digital investment despite strong demand ([assessment](2026-08-28-cmr-ecofinagency-us-digital-investment-obstacles)).

2026-01 - a [syndicated financing of FCFA 44.884bn for densification, desaturation and extension of the mobile network was consolidated and signed at Yaounde](2026-01-22-camtel-cbc-44-884bn-fcfa-mobile-network-expansion-techafricanews). It is unreconciled against a separately carried January 2026 package figure, and no site, coverage or disbursement figure is published.

The [US$225m three-year capital pledge, the single largest private commitment in the tracked non-state set, is an announcement with no instrument and no reporting against it](2025-01-01-mtn-cameroon-cmr-2025-network-capex-pledge-bw03), and no disbursement or drawdown was recorded in the window.

2026-03-04 - the [state pension fund signed a capital-participation protocol behind a build-operate-transfer smart-port concession agreed with the port authority in November 2025](2026-03-04-leconomie-cnps-innovendi-smart-port), with no investment amount, share or schedule published.

summary: A [US$29m trade-finance guarantee was approved](2025-12-03-afdb-29m-cca-bank-telecoms-funding-itweb) and a [pandemic-preparedness project launched with FCFA 13.44bn](2026-08-01-pandemic-fund-cmr-2026-record).
developments:
2025-12 - a development bank board [approved a US$29m transaction guarantee to a Cameroonian bank, a portion earmarked for telecom equipment purchase](2025-12-03-afdb-29m-cca-bank-telecoms-funding-itweb). The [telecom share is not quantified](2025-01-01-african-development-bank-cca-bank-2025-cameroon-trade-finance-bw06), so the digital portion is unestablished.

2026-07-29 - a [preparedness project was launched with FCFA 13.44bn from the fund inside an envelope of FCFA 91.5bn, running 2026 to 2029, to digitise community surveillance in 42 municipalities, stand up seven regional emergency call centres and increase interoperability of the national health information systems](2026-08-01-pandemic-fund-cmr-2026-record), with co-financing of FCFA 64.05bn and national co-investment of FCFA 13.83bn. No deliverable is reported.

summary: The regulator's 2024 observatory records [over 15m internet subscriptions, 99% of them mobile, with data traffic up 26%](2025-12-09-art-2024-annual-observatory-telecom-market-techafricanews).
developments:
The regulator's 2024 annual market observatory records [over 15m internet subscriptions, 99% of them mobile, data traffic up 26%, fixed teledensity described as extremely low, and over 11m active mobile financial services subscribers](2025-12-09-art-2024-annual-observatory-telecom-market-techafricanews).

The account held is secondary; the regulator's own report is not. The base holds no comparable dated prior-year subscription figure and no penetration or gender-gap rate at all, so the only movement statable is the traffic growth, and the level is carried as the observatory states it rather than promoted into a current position.

summary: The backbone is [reported at over 15,000 km](2026-07-27-cameroon-starlink-licensing-stalls-sovereignty), and a [fourth phase of about FCFA 108.4bn was authorised by decree](2026-03-11-leconomie-china-eximbank-fibre-backbone-phase4-loan).
developments:
The base held [about 12,000 km terrestrial plus about 812 km overhead on 2024 reference-year figures](2025-12-09-art-2024-annual-observatory-telecom-market-techafricanews), and the backbone is now [reported at over 15,000 km](2026-07-27-cameroon-starlink-licensing-stalls-sovereignty). The two figures are not reconciled to a single primary and may rest on different measurement bases.

2026-03-06 - a decree [authorised signature of CNY 1,350,963,161, about FCFA 108.4bn, for a further 4,000 km, a national data centre and regional links to Chad, the Central African Republic and Nigeria](2026-03-11-leconomie-china-eximbank-fibre-backbone-phase4-loan). The [loan is not confirmed signed](2026-01-01-eximbank-cn-cmr-006-cameroon-fibre-optic-transmission-backbone-extension) and the executing contractor is not confirmed.

summary: A [memorandum to join the Medusa Africa submarine cable was finalised in December 2025](2025-12-10-ecofinagency-cameroon-medusa-africa-submarine-cable-mou).
developments:
[Cameroon finalised a memorandum of understanding to join the Medusa Africa submarine cable project, stated to be operational by 2028 and to improve connectivity with Europe, Africa and Asia](2025-12-10-ecofinagency-cameroon-medusa-africa-submarine-cable-mou).

It is a memorandum and not a landing: no landing station, capacity, cost or in-service date for Cameroon is held.

summary: CAMIX [opened a third point of presence at the ST Digital data centre in April 2026](2026-04-07-camix-troisieme-pop-st-digital).
developments:
[CAMIX opened a third point of presence at the ST Digital data centre in April 2026](2026-04-07-camix-troisieme-pop-st-digital). [Its Douala presence is tracked in the Internet Society's register](2026-08-01-isoc-pulse-camix-douala-tracker), and [the exchange's own site dates its current form to March 2026](2026-03-16-camix-site-officiel).

No peering-member count, traffic figure or local-traffic share is held.

progress: Movement, a draft concession convention was finalised while the file stayed undecided and the seizure circular stayed operative
summary: A [draft concession convention was finalised in December 2025](2025-12-12-cmr-starlink-convention-concession-art), with the [file at the ministry undecided for more than two years](2026-07-27-cameroon-starlink-licensing-stalls-sovereignty).
developments:
The [licence was refused in March 2025](2025-03-08-cmr-refus-licence-starlink). 2025-12-12 - the regulator [finalised a draft concession convention and specification](2025-12-12-cmr-starlink-convention-concession-art), and as at July 2026 the [file at the ministry had been undecided for more than two years, with the objections on record being lawful interception, armed-group use and the incumbent's commercial position](2026-07-27-cameroon-starlink-licensing-stalls-sovereignty).

The [2024 customs circular remains the operative instrument, with kits entering through indirect registration abroad and ten modems seized at one post on 12 December 2025](2025-12-16-cameroon-douane-saisie-kits-starlink). No other satellite broadband offer is on file, so the country's whole position on the technology is one undecided file and a seizure regime.

progress: No change, a first position with no earlier figure behind it
summary: A United States company [stated an intention to invest US$75m](2026-08-29-cameroon-cybastion-douala-ai-data-centre) in an artificial-intelligence data centre and power plant at Douala.
developments:
The intention was announced on 27 August 2026 at the inaugural bilateral economic and commercial dialogue, as one project among an estimated US$7bn of investment and trade opportunities floated there ([announcement](2026-08-29-cameroon-cybastion-douala-ai-data-centre)).

No agreement, site, capacity, financing arrangement or date is on record, and the pairing of a data centre with its own power plant is the part worth noting: the developer is proposing to supply the power rather than to draw it. The national provider's own facility is recorded separately.

2026-09-07 - the announced Douala project was confirmed and qualified in the same week. The vendor [confirmed US$75m, about FCFA 42.25bn, for a data centre designed in part for artificial-intelligence workloads with dedicated power generation](2026-09-04-cmr-biometricupdate-cybastion-sovereignty), while the [planning ministry described it as an intention presented at the first bilateral economic forum rather than a commitment](2026-09-07-cmr-businessincameroon-cybastion-75m). The same vendor's [Cote d'Ivoire project was underwritten by a US$66.14m export-credit guarantee](2026-09-07-cmr-businessincameroon-cybastion-75m); nothing of that kind is published here.

summary: The [Zamengoe data centre is in operation and being shown to prospective tenants](2026-08-14-cameroon-camtel-zamengoe-data-centre), the central bank having inspected it in December 2025.
developments:
The base carries no record of the facility before December 2025, when the [regional central bank's national director inspected it with a view to hosting](2025-12-17-beac-national-director-visits-camtel-data-center-techreviewafrica).

2026-06-09 - it was [presented at a national digital forum as in operation and tourable](2026-06-12-camtel-zamengoe-data-centre-sovereignty-sago-techreviewafrica), and on [13 August 2026 a second prospective tenant was shown round](2026-08-14-camtel-showcases-zamengoe-data-center-to-plan-international-cameroon).

The largest-in-Central-Africa and Tier III claims are unverified wire claims and are not adopted here. No IT load, floor area, customer count or contracted power figure has been published, and no tenancy is reported signed.

summary: A [nationwide smart-meter deployment launched on 27 May 2026](2026-05-29-rollout-20000-smart-meters-ami-world-bank-wearetech), with a meter-data centre under construction at Douala.
developments:
At the window's opening the [electricity-reform programme was financed with no meters deployed](2024-01-01-world-bank-cmr-2024-prsec-electricity-reform-bw12).

2026-05-27 - [20,000 advanced meters began deploying in phases after trials in January and February 2026 and final acceptance in April, with a meter-data centre being built at Douala to centralise and secure the data](2026-05-29-rollout-20000-smart-meters-ami-world-bank-wearetech). The programme runs 2024 to 2026 at about FCFA 400bn, of which FCFA 180bn is World Bank and FCFA 48bn African Development Bank.

The data centre's operator, capacity and cost are not published, and no outage, loss or collection figure has been reported against the deployment.

progress: Mixed, the incident response team was hardened and the national zone stays signed while the DNSSEC validation target passed unmet and IPv6 has no target at all
summary: The [incident response team was equipped in January 2026](2026-01-21-antic-cirt-cybersecurity-systems-patnuc-techafricanews), while [DNSSEC validation sits at 56.60% against a target that has passed](2025-12-09-leconomie-antic-dnssec-rpki-cyberspace-defence).
developments:
2026-01-20 - [intrusion-detection and prevention hardware and software were commissioned for the national incident response team at about FCFA 735m under the national connectivity project; the team ingests about 200GB a day and runs the national key infrastructure](2026-01-21-antic-cirt-cybersecurity-systems-patnuc-techafricanews), having [identified and blocked 19m threats in 2024](2025-02-13-lejour-19-million-cyber-threats-blocked-2024). The [national zone has been cryptographically signed since April 2025](2026-06-19-antic-national-dns-forum-sovereign-internet-techafricanews).

2026-09-04 - the gap between the statute and the threat was measured from outside government: a policy institute's brief puts [cyberattacks up 156% between 2020 and 2023, financial losses from digital fraud above US$45m over the same period, and the national ICT agency's cybercrime unit at 23% of its establishment](2026-09-04-cmr-nkafu-cybersecurity-industrial-policy), arguing that cybersecurity belongs in the national development strategy as industrial policy. The figures are the institute's own.

progress: No change, still a demand rather than an instrument
summary: Forum participants [pressed for a national interoperability infrastructure in August 2026](2026-08-21-biometricupdate-cameroon-national-interoperability-infrastructure); none exists.
developments:
[Participants from government, the private sector and civil society at the 2026 Cameroon Internet Governance Forum, held under the theme of moving from fragmentation to interoperability, pressed for the establishment of a national interoperability infrastructure](2026-08-21-biometricupdate-cameroon-national-interoperability-infrastructure).

It is a stakeholder demand and not a government commitment: no instrument, budget line or implementing agency follows from it on the record.

summary: A [biometric payroll system had flagged over 53,000 public servants drawing undue benefits by June 2026](2026-08-10-cameroon-fake-birth-certificates-payroll-fraud-census).
developments:
The system has been [operational since early 2025 and had flagged more than 53,000 public servants drawing undue benefits by June 2026, on the public service minister's statement to parliament, and now runs alongside a separate finance ministry census of more than 950,000 dependent-child birth certificates](2026-08-10-cameroon-fake-birth-certificates-payroll-fraud-census). Payroll fraud through forged or duplicate birth certificates was unchecked before it.

It is the clearest use of identity data by another system on this ledger, and it points back at the civil register: the fraud it detects is a civil-registration failure, and the remedy on file is a manual census of nearly a million certificates rather than a register fix.

summary: A [pandemic-preparedness project launched in July 2026 includes increasing interoperability of the national health information systems](2026-08-01-pandemic-fund-cmr-2026-record).
developments:
2026-07-29 - the project was [launched to digitise community surveillance in 42 municipalities, stand up seven regional emergency call centres and increase interoperability of the national health information systems, running 2026 to 2029](2026-08-01-pandemic-fund-cmr-2026-record).

Nothing is reported delivered against any of the three. The base holds no inventory of the health information systems that would be made interoperable, no standard they would meet, and no baseline of how they exchange data now, so the project's interoperability component has nothing measurable behind it yet.

summary: [4,000 free cards were delivered at Yaounde 5, some to people blocked for over fifteen years by duplicate-identity records](2026-07-27-cameroon-yaounde-5-national-id-cards-delivered).
developments:
2026-07-27 - [4,000 free cards were delivered in one district, some to recipients blocked for over fifteen years by duplicate-identity records, cleared by seconding police officers on site](2026-07-27-cameroon-yaounde-5-national-id-cards-delivered). The delivery was timed to public-service and police recruitment competitions, for which the card is a precondition.

What it shows is a register carrying duplicate-identity records that block real people from real entitlements, and a remedy applied by posting officers to one district rather than by correcting the register. No count of blocked records, no national clearance programme and no deduplication figure has been published.

summary: A [second production centre opened at Garoua in August 2025](2025-08-07-new-biometric-id-card-center-garoua-northern-cameroon-biometricupdate), running at about 2,000 cards a day.
developments:
Issuance ran from a single production centre at the window's opening, the [new card having entered issuance in March 2025](2025-03-05-issuance-of-new-national-id-card-takes-off-biometricupdate).

2025-08-07 - a [second centre opened at Garoua at about 2,000 cards a day, with a displacement-response enrolment track](2025-08-07-new-biometric-id-card-center-garoua-northern-cameroon-biometricupdate).

No enrolment total, coverage rate or backlog figure has been published at either end, so production capacity is the only measure of registration the base holds - and capacity is not coverage.

summary: The card is produced under a [fifteen-year build-operate-transfer contract signed in May 2024](2025-03-05-issuance-of-new-national-id-card-takes-off-biometricupdate), with a FCFA 10,000 pre-enrolment fee.
developments:
The credential is produced under a [fifteen-year build-operate-transfer contract signed in May 2024, with a pre-enrolment fee of FCFA 10,000](2025-03-05-issuance-of-new-national-id-card-takes-off-biometricupdate), and nothing in the window changed that arrangement.

The same pattern runs through the consular credential, issued under a [ten-year build-operate-transfer contract signed in April 2022](2025-12-10-impact-palmares-digital-visa-deal-printing-contract-biometricupdate). No transfer milestone, revenue share, performance standard or exit arrangement is published for either, so what the state will own at the end of fifteen years is not stated anywhere on file.

progress: Mixed, routine issuance began in ten municipalities while a one-million-pupil registration drive missed its target and restarts
summary: [Digital birth certificates entered routine issuance across ten municipalities in three regions](2026-01-12-councils-begin-issuance-digital-birth-certificates-biometricupdate) from January 2026. A [drive to reach one million primary-school pupils holding no certificate was found far from its target and restarts in September 2026](2026-08-31-cameroon-birth-registration-drive-schools-legal-identity).
developments:
The certificates were [provided for in the 2024 civil-registration law with none issued](2026-01-12-councils-begin-issuance-digital-birth-certificates-biometricupdate) at the window's opening. The first was issued at a Limbe council in January 2026, and issuance is now [routine across ten municipalities in three regions, with the same legal worth as physical certificates](2026-01-13 Cameroon intros digital system for civil documents).

2026-08-07 - equipment for [three pilot centres digitising civil-status registration went out to tender by the United Nations development programme, the centres, their locations, the value and the timetable not named](2026-08-07-cameroon-undp-civil-status-digitisation-equipment). Three pilot centres is the whole of that scope, against a register the base elsewhere records being used to draw fraudulent payroll claims.

2026-08-26 — a drive launched in 2024 to reach one million pupils holding no birth certificate was [found far from its target, and the Basic Education minister ordered pupils' files submitted to the courts before 15 September, restarting mobile court hearings from September](2026-08-31-cameroon-birth-registration-drive-schools-legal-identity). No count of certificates issued under the 2024 drive is published, so the shortfall is stated and not measured. The court route is not discretionary: the law requires a declaratory judgment wherever the 90-day deadline was missed.

summary: An [implementation partner was engaged for civil-registration digitisation with a 2029 target, to integrate with the biometric card and the voter kits](2025-10-27 Cameroon's BUNEC partners with Liber Technologies for CRVS digitization).
developments:
No implementation partner was named at the window's opening. In October 2025 one was [engaged, with a fully digital target for 2029 and a stated intention to integrate with the biometric identity card and the voter enrolment kits](2025-10-27 Cameroon's BUNEC partners with Liber Technologies for CRVS digitization).

That is the only stated link between civil registration and the identity credential anywhere on this ledger, and it is an intention with a four-year horizon rather than a built interface. No design, standard, milestone or interim deliverable has been published, and the event date is month-precision only.

summary: [Compulsory taxi and driver registration opened at Yaounde with a QR code per driver](2026-07-01-digital-id-system-taxi-owners-drivers-biometricupdate), and a [student digital identity was provided for](2026-06-11-student-digital-id-program-mtn-biometricupdate).
developments:
2026-07-03 to 2026-10-05 - [compulsory registration on a city platform opened, with a QR code and a unique door number per driver, unregistered taxis barred after the deadline](2026-07-01-digital-id-system-taxi-owners-drivers-biometricupdate). It is a city council order with development-agency support.

2026-06 - a memorandum addendum [provided for a secondary-school student digital identity card linked to academic, financial and disciplinary records and to school-fee payment, replacing a unique student identification number assigned through a ministry portal since 2024](2026-06-11-student-digital-id-program-mtn-biometricupdate); no issuance is reported and no signature date is published.

Neither is stated to draw on the national register, so both are sectoral credentials rather than uses of the foundational identity.

summary: A [tariff-grid revision went to consultation at Douala on 30 July 2026](2026-07-30-cemac-gimacpay-transactions-2025), the operator conceding that pricing penalises low-value transactions.
developments:
2026-07-30 to 31 - a consultation workshop opened and closed on revising the regional switch's tariff grid, [the operator conceding that current pricing penalises low-value transactions and drives artificial splitting of payments](2026-07-30-cemac-gimacpay-transactions-2025).

No revised grid, effective date or fee schedule has been published. Pricing that penalises small payments is the mechanism by which an interoperable rail stays a large-ticket rail, which the merchant-payment figures elsewhere in this report show it currently is; the consultation is the first acknowledgement of it on file.

summary: An [order of 28 May 2025 made the Treasury platform the only lawful channel for non-tax revenue](2025-06-05-cameroon-mandates-digital-payment-platform-non-tax-revenues), and device duties moved onto the customs platform.
developments:
2025-05-28 - an order [made the Treasury's platform the only lawful channel for collecting non-tax revenue, giving named departments three months to use it exclusively, accepting mobile money, bank cards and post-office counter payments with receipt authentication and real-time tracking, against a 2025 non-tax revenue target of FCFA 361bn on an estimated potential of nearly FCFA 600bn](2025-06-05-cameroon-mandates-digital-payment-platform-non-tax-revenues). Nothing reports compliance after the deadline.

2026-04-01 - [importers must declare each device by its identifier through the customs platform and pay duties before network use, with an amnesty for devices connected before that date, customs putting annual losses from undeclared devices at about US$21.5m](2026-04-01-imei-system-mobile-device-import-duties-camcis-techcabal). Enforcement follows: [deactivation of handsets on which duty has not been paid begins 1 September 2026 under a communique of 20 August 2026, after an earlier date of 25 May 2026 was abandoned when operators objected that no test phase had preceded a full-scale deployment](2026-08-24-cameroun-blocage-telephones-non-dedouanes-consensus). A [card for fully digital settlement of customs duties was reported as about to be signed in March 2026](2026-03-30-leconomie-digital-customs-payment-tool), with no launch date on file.

summary: Interoperable merchant payments ran at [48,605 transactions worth FCFA 9.7bn in the first quarter of 2026](2026-08-01-leconomie-paiement-marchand-interoperable-cemac-premier-trimestre-2026), under 1% of switch volume.
developments:
The first-quarter 2026 acquiring and issuing tables record [48,605 transactions worth FCFA 9.7bn, under 1% of the switch's 2025 volume, at an average ticket of FCFA 199,485 against FCFA 42,512 across all flows](2026-08-01-leconomie-paiement-marchand-interoperable-cemac-premier-trimestre-2026).

The concentration is extreme: [two mobile operators together account for 98% of issuing value and one bank for 71% of acquiring value](2026-08-01-leconomie-paiement-marchand-interoperable-cemac-premier-trimestre-2026). A merchant rail with an average ticket nearly five times the all-flows average is being used for large payments between businesses rather than for retail acceptance, which is what the tariff consultation concedes.

summary: An [interoperable QR-code standard launched at Douala in July 2026](2026-07-30-cemac-gimac-norme-qr-code-interoperable) lets any wallet or bank application scan any merchant code.
developments:
2026-07-29 - the standard [went live so that any bank, microfinance or mobile-money application can scan any merchant code across the six member states, routed and settled through the regional switch](2026-07-30-cemac-gimac-norme-qr-code-interoperable). No count of merchants or applications on it has been published since.

The state operator's own wallet, [launched on 1 May 2025, has never published a subscriber, wallet or transaction figure](2025-05-02-lejour-camtel-blue-money-launch-announced) and [was still without one in December 2025](2025-12-23-lejour-camtel-ethio-telecom-blue-money), so the one nationally owned retail payment instrument on this ledger cannot be assessed at all.

2026-08-31 — a domestic technology company [launched a payments platform carrying transfers across mobile-money networks, wallet management, bill and airtime payment, payment links and developer interfaces](2026-08-31-techafricanews-lbpay-cameroon). It is a launch announcement on the company's own account: no user, merchant or transaction figure, licence or partner bank is named.

summary: The regional switch carried [20.3m transactions worth FCFA 863bn in 2025, up 40% by volume](2026-07-30-cemac-gimacpay-transactions-2025), across 153 participants.
developments:
The switch carried [about 14.5m transactions worth about FCFA 710bn in 2024](2025-10-20-lejour-gimacpay-600bn-fcfa-transactions), and [20.3m transactions worth FCFA 863bn in 2025, up 40% by volume, across 153 participants, with 84.33m transactions worth FCFA 3,624bn cumulative since service start](2026-07-30-cemac-gimacpay-transactions-2025).

The figures are regional, not Cameroonian. The nearest national measure is the regulator's count of [over 11m active mobile financial services subscribers in 2024](2025-12-09-art-2024-annual-observatory-telecom-market-techafricanews), with no comparable prior-year figure held, so national uptake is a level rather than a movement.

summary: The [regional central bank joined the pan-African settlement system in July 2026](2026-07-09-beac-joins-papss-cross-border-payments-cemac-techafricanews), extending it to all six member states.
developments:
2026-07-09 - the regional central bank [joined the pan-African settlement system, extending it to all six member states and 72m people and taking the network to 28 countries and sixteen switches](2026-07-09-beac-joins-papss-cross-border-payments-cemac-techafricanews), with [member-state banks to be integrated by the end of 2026](2026-07-10-beac-joins-papss-cemac-banks-agenceecofin).

No Cameroonian bank is yet named as live on the rail, no corridor volume or value is published, and nothing states the pricing or settlement arrangement a Cameroonian institution would face. Membership is an accession, not a working corridor.

summary: The [financial-literacy project closed on 15 July 2026 leaving its comparison platform with no funded data-update mechanism](2026-07-24-finance-4-all-senegal-education-financiere-numerique).
developments:
2026-07-15 - the digital financial-literacy project running since June 2024 [closed, leaving a digital financial-services comparison platform with no funded data-update mechanism, offered to both participating states and neither reported as having accepted](2026-07-24-finance-4-all-senegal-education-financiere-numerique). No Cameroon-side trainee count, budget share or partner list is published.

The separate [bank-fee comparison platform launched in June 2025 covers commercial banks only, and neither committed extension has been recorded as delivered](2025-06-23-cnef-bankcompar-financial-literacy-platform-itweb): a savings simulator promised by end-2025 and extension to microfinance and insurance promised for 2026 are both unverified.

summary: Tenders to digitalise civil registration [in Bamenda](2026-08-10-pnud-bamenda-appel-offre-digitalisation-etat-civil) and [the East region](2026-08-25-undp-bertoua-sigec-digitalisation-etat-civil-est) were issued in August 2026.
developments:
[UNDP issued a tender in August 2026 to digitalise civil registration through the SIGEC system in the East region at Bertoua](2026-08-25-undp-bertoua-sigec-digitalisation-etat-civil-est), and [a companion tender covers Bamenda](2026-08-10-pnud-bamenda-appel-offre-digitalisation-etat-civil). [Integration of civil registration with identity systems was argued for in May 2026](2026-05-18-cameroon-tribune-integrate-civil-registration-id-systems).

[The statistics institute has published civil-status statistics for 2018 to 2022](2023-08-01-ins-cameroun-rapport-statistiques-etat-civil-2018-2022). No national registration rate after 2022 and no coverage figure for the digitalisation is held.

summary: A [bank partnership made a certified geolocated postal address a condition of account opening](2025-06-19-cameroons-findme-rides-new-bank-deal-scale-digital-addressing), reaching more than 700,000 clients.
developments:
[About 15,000 addresses had been generated since a 2024 postal-operator agreement underpinning the national postal location plan](2025-06-19-cameroons-findme-rides-new-bank-deal-scale-digital-addressing).

2025-06-19 - a [bank partnership required every new customer to supply a geolocated postal address certified through the startup's postal-operator tie-up, reaching more than 700,000 clients of that bank, at FCFA 2,000 a certification](2025-06-19-cameroons-findme-rides-new-bank-deal-scale-digital-addressing).

It is a privately run register entering the identity-verification stack without a legislative act. No address count since, no coverage figure, no data-controller arrangement and no obligation on the operator to serve anyone who will not pay the fee are on file.

summary: The [unified social registry stands where it was appraised in February 2022](2022-02-14-cameroon-adaptive-safety-nets-economic-inclusion-pad-p175363), with nothing on file since on what has been built.
developments:
The registry is [provided for under the adaptive safety nets and economic inclusion project, whose component on shock-responsive digital delivery systems - a social registry and a digital payments system - is appraised at US$5m equivalent, with safety nets estimated to reach 25% of the poor population](2022-02-14-cameroon-adaptive-safety-nets-economic-inclusion-pad-p175363), [as set out at project identification](2022-01-04-cameroon-adaptive-safety-nets-economic-inclusion-project-pid-p175363).

Nothing on file since appraisal reports what has been built. Later reporting on the registry is in the base but is not citable, so the position stated here is four years old and older than the record.

summary: A [register of about 8.2 million voters went through deduplication before the October 2025 vote](2025-09-11-cameroon-signals-urgency-biometric-voter-id-collection), with hundreds of thousands of cards uncollected.
developments:
The register ran on third-generation kits at the window's opening, the elections board having [acquired a thousand biometric enrolment kits](2025-05-08-lejour-elecam-acquires-1000-biometric-enrolment-kits).

2025-09-11 - [about 8.2 million voters were under deduplication ahead of the 12 October presidential vote, with hundreds of thousands of biometric cards uncollected - more than 350,000 in the Littoral region, about 50,000 of 115,000 collected in the South, 31,861 of 66,515 distributed in the South West - some printed in 2018 or earlier, the board warning that a registered voter without a card cannot vote](2025-09-11-cameroon-signals-urgency-biometric-voter-id-collection).

No post-election collection figure, deduplication result or audit is on file.

progress: Mixed, a Douala cadastre memorandum was signed while the lands ministry's own cadastre line was cut 44.2%
summary: A [memorandum of 28 April 2026 covers about 200,000 land files and a digital possession certificate](2026-05-07-leconomie-douala-digital-land-registry-possession-certificate), while the [budget line fell](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-37-380).
developments:
2026-04-28 - a memorandum was signed to [digitise about 200,000 land files at Douala, with a digital possession certificate, and no budget, timeline or start date published](2026-05-07-leconomie-douala-digital-land-registry-possession-certificate).

The money went the other way. The lands ministry's cadastre modernisation programme was [tabled at FCFA 874,046,000 for FY2026 against FCFA 1,567,500,000 appropriated for FY2025](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-37-380), a 44.2% cut and below the FY2024 level, at proposed stage only. It is the only digital line outside the sector vote, so the cut is the whole of the state's own cadastre financing story.

summary: A [national digital health strategic plan for 2026-2030 was launched on 4 March 2026](2026-03-04-minsante-plan-strategique-national-sante-numerique-2026-2030).
developments:
[The health ministry's Plan strategique national de sante numerique 2026-2030 was launched on 4 March 2026 in French](2026-03-04-minsante-plan-strategique-national-sante-numerique-2026-2030), with [an English implementation framework and monitoring companion](2026-01-01-minsante-plan-strategique-sante-numerique-2026-2030).

The capture reaches the contents and drafting-committee lists and not the substantive chapters, so no commitment, target or budget from the plan can be stated.

summary: [EUR 8m of technical assistance was agreed for the education information system and database interconnection](2026-07-31-cameroon-unesco-basic-education-agreement-websig-database-interconnection), and [examinations digitisation was agreed](2026-01-19-camtel-baccalaureate-office-digitize-national-exams-techafricanews).
developments:
2026-07 - a technical-assistance agreement covers [EUR 8m over 36 months across the education management information system, the basic-education ministry's mapping platform, interconnection of the education databases and dynamic dashboards](2026-07-31-cameroon-unesco-basic-education-agreement-websig-database-interconnection). Nothing is reported delivered, the funder is not stated and the signature date is not published.

2026-01-15 - a partnership agreed [three pillars for national examinations: site interconnection, examination data in the sovereign national cloud, and examination-management platforms](2026-01-19-camtel-baccalaureate-office-digitize-national-exams-techafricanews). Nothing is reported live, and the sovereign national cloud the data would sit in has not itself moved in the window.

summary: [42 court registries were on terminals against a target of 60 by end-2025](2025-09-30-cameroon-justice-system-slow-progress-despite-reforms-since-2018), and a [fourth video-surveillance tranche was authorised](2025-12-23-lejour-urban-videosurveillance-loan).
developments:
The court-management system was [launched after plans to import a neighbouring country's system were dropped, backed by US$10m from the African Development Bank, with 42 court registries on terminals linked to the secure judicial network against a target of 60 by the end of 2025](2025-09-30-cameroon-justice-system-slow-progress-despite-reforms-since-2018). No later count is held, so whether the target was met is unestablished.

2025-12-17 - a decree [authorised a fourth video-surveillance tranche of FCFA 39.2bn, bringing FCFA 150.8bn mobilised over eight years across three Chinese lenders](2025-12-23-lejour-urban-videosurveillance-loan); the [first phase's borrower was the defence ministry and delivered 1,500 cameras and 2,000 portable radios](2026-07-22-aiddata-58535-bank-of-china-cameroon-video-surveillance-phase1), on accounts that disagree about amounts and dates.

summary: An [integrated tax and duty management system was contracted on 10 April 2026 at about FCFA 4.7bn](2026-05-07-cameroon-awards-tax-digitalization-contract-international-consortium-sigit), specified to interoperate with customs, budget and treasury.
developments:
A tax directorate information-systems modernisation programme had run [since 2018 with no integrated system contracted](2026-05-13-leconomie-tax-digitalisation-dgi).

2026-04-10 - the system was [contracted to a consortium of two Tunisian, one Canadian and one Cameroonian firm at EUR 5.997m excluding tax and EUR 7.15m including it, about FCFA 4.7bn, over 24 months, financed by KfW, after a restricted international tender opened on 24 February 2025 and the lender's no-objection of 7 April 2026, and is specified to interoperate with customs, budget and treasury systems](2026-05-07-cameroon-awards-tax-digitalization-contract-international-consortium-sigit).

It is the most precisely documented digital procurement on this ledger. Nothing is reported delivered against the 24 months.

progress: Mixed, a trilateral customs committee was established while the audit chamber found the trade single window and the collection agencies do not reconcile
summary: A [trilateral customs steering committee was established on 29 July 2026](2026-07-29-cameroon-nigeria-benin-customs-border-cooperation), while the [audit chamber found no cross-checking against the trade single window](2026-07-30-cameroon-audit-chamber-forests-mines-customs-single-window-do-not-interoperate).
developments:
2026-07-29 - a joint communique [established a trilateral steering committee with commitments to harmonised procedures, digital interoperability and coordinated risk management on two named corridors](2026-07-29-cameroon-nigeria-benin-customs-border-cooperation); no timeline, budget or system specification is published.

Against that, the audit chamber [recorded discrepancies between revenues declared by the forestry, mining and customs administrations and the amounts registered in the trade single window, and no cross-checking mechanism between the two, naming reconciliation as a workstream for the 2025 certification campaign with no compliance timetable set](2026-07-30-cameroon-audit-chamber-forests-mines-customs-single-window-do-not-interoperate). The window is the reference platform for tracking trade-related financial flows, so the finding goes to what it is for.

summary: [Second-generation consular services launched across 46 posts](2026-05-08-lejour-evisa-540000-visas-three-years), and a [utility commercial platform entered rollout](2026-08-16-cameroon-camwater-wateris-digital-ecosystem).
developments:
The consular platform carried entry visas online only at the window's opening; second-generation consular cards and travel documents [launched in October 2025 and the platform now runs across 46 consular posts and two international airports](2026-05-08-lejour-evisa-540000-visas-three-years).

2026-08-10 to 14 - the water utility [trained staff ahead of rollout of a centralised platform replacing decentralised commercial management, with automated meter reading and expanded electronic payment channels](2026-08-16-cameroon-camwater-wateris-digital-ecosystem); the account is the director general's and no customer count, cost or completion date is stated.

The [electronic public-procurement platform runs on a US$12m grant-funded upgrade with no dated update](2025-06-30-coleps-digital-procurement-korean-grant-biometricupdate), a further US$12.5m for interoperability described as due in 2026 and unconfirmed.

progress: Movement, on a FCFA 92bn programme with no financier, instrument or start date
summary: [230 councils, about 64%, are supported by the ICT agency](2026-07-16-antic-urges-north-west-councils-digital-transformation-techafricanews), and a [FCFA 92bn digitisation programme was presented to partners](2026-06-04-digi-cor-163m-digitize-local-governments-wearetech).
developments:
2026-07-16 - agency figures put [230 councils, about 64% nationally, under its support, 48.6% of North West councils operating functional websites, 335 municipal portals developed and 145 authorities equipped](2026-07-16-antic-urges-north-west-councils-digital-transformation-techafricanews).

2026-06-02 - a [FCFA 92bn local-government digitisation programme was presented to technical and financial partners with no financier, no signed instrument and no start date](2026-06-04-digi-cor-163m-digitize-local-governments-wearetech). It [follows a July 2025 digital master plan for about 394 decentralised authorities, against the government's own baseline that 68.5% lack structured computer networks and 57.8% employ no digitally trained staff](2026-06-04-digi-cor-163m-digitize-local-governments-wearetech).

The water utility awarded a Chinese manufacturer a [FCFA 721.76m contract on 17 August 2026 to deploy 3,000 smart meters, the first 7.5 per cent of the 40,000 planned under a World Bank-financed programme](2026-09-04-cmr-camwater-3000-compteurs-intelligents-laison). No installation schedule, data-handling arrangement or tariff effect is stated, and the meters read household consumption.

progress: Mixed, a rail detection system entered service and school simulations were adopted while the rail customer portal's target quarter passed with nothing on record
summary: A [forward-detection system is in service on locomotives](2025-11-24-leconomie-camrail-ai-rail-safety), and the [secondary-education ministry adopted generated simulations](2026-08-19-dba-minesec-simulation-ia-e-education).
developments:
2025-11-24 - a [forward-detection system was presented as deployed on locomotives, detecting people, obstacles and crossings to 2 km against a 1.5 km maximum braking distance](2025-11-24-leconomie-camrail-ai-rail-safety); no fleet count or contract value is published.

2026-08-17 - the secondary-education ministry [formally adopted generated simulations for use in schools, saying it produced more than 250 in under a month at no cost, with teacher demonstrations in chemistry, biology, languages and industrial techniques](2026-08-19-dba-minesec-simulation-ia-e-education). The production count and the zero-cost claim are the ministry's own, and no pedagogical evaluation, accuracy check or distribution route to schools without connectivity is published.

The [intelligent customer portal announced for first-quarter 2026 delivery, with a wagon-allocation decision algorithm as its centrepiece, has nothing on record after November 2025](2025-11-24-leconomie-camrail-ai-rail-safety).

progress: Mixed, a high-performance computing centre and a sovereign scientific database were named as priorities while the sovereign language model and the GPU hosting node did not move
summary: A [national high-performance computing centre was named to cabinet as a priority](2026-07-31-cameroon-pm-national-ai-strategy-completion), while the [sovereign language model has no build, budget or partner](2025-07-08-snia-2040-ai-roadmap-seven-pillars-techafricanews).
developments:
2026-07-30 - cabinet was told of a [national high-performance computing centre among ten priority areas, with no site, cost, operator or timetable published](2026-07-31-cameroon-pm-national-ai-strategy-completion), and of a [sovereign scientific database on a dedicated national platform and a centre for the digitisation of scientific and technical information, neither with a cost, site or timeline](2026-07-31-cameroon-government-engages-on-harnessing-ai).

The [sovereign large language model for national languages, named in the roadmap's third pillar, has no build, budget, partner or corpus named in any held source since July 2025](2025-07-08-snia-2040-ai-roadmap-seven-pillars-techafricanews). The [GPU hosting node announced in February 2025 for a second-quarter start is confirmed in service by no held source, and the company's May 2026 profile does not mention it](2026-05-13-anthony-same-st-digital-african-datacenter-network-wearetech) - the only domestic compute of its kind in the base.

summary: Sector revenue reached [FCFA 1,022bn in 2024, up 18%, with investment up 35%](2025-12-09-art-2024-annual-observatory-telecom-market-techafricanews), and a [local software suite launched](2026-06-15-leconomie-kmr-pyramid-local-storage-digital-ecosystem).
developments:
The regulator's 2024 observatory records [FCFA 1,022bn of sector revenue, up 18%, investment of FCFA 194.5bn, up 35%, 3.16% of GDP and 31.5m active mobile subscriptions](2025-12-09-art-2024-annual-observatory-telecom-market-techafricanews). The account is secondary; the regulator's own report is not held.

2026-06-10 - a [locally built software suite launched with a browser and mail service available and a media service still being finalised, two years' build at a stated FCFA 20m and more, hosted on domestic infrastructure](2026-06-15-leconomie-kmr-pyramid-local-storage-digital-ecosystem). The cost is promoter-reported, and no user, download or revenue figure is published.

summary: A [climate innovation hub launched at a Yaounde university](2025-10-09-camcih-climate-innovation-hub-green-tech-wearetech), and a [sixth digital centre opened in the Far North](2026-05-10-orange-cameroon-sixth-digital-center-maroua-techreviewafrica).
developments:
2025-10-02 - an [incubation and collaboration platform launched at a Yaounde university for renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, waste and urban resilience, with no budget, cohort or funding figure published](2025-10-09-camcih-climate-innovation-hub-green-tech-wearetech).

2026-05 - an operator [inaugurated a sixth centre at a Far North university, with 481 young people trained and 50 international certifications issued since technical opening](2026-05-10-orange-cameroon-sixth-digital-center-maroua-techreviewafrica). The training figures are the company's own and unaudited, the source is a wire item, and no dated prior count of centres is held, so the sixth is dated and the first five are not.

progress: Movement, on two funded ventures raising US$300,000 in the year
summary: A [national funding-match platform launched in January 2026](2026-01-27-proxigab-national-digital-platform-smes-techafricanews), against [two funded startups raising US$300,000 in 2025](2026-02-03-disrupt-africa-african-tech-startups-funding-report-2025).
developments:
2026-01-22 - the trade ministry [launched a national platform matching small businesses and young entrepreneurs to national and international funding, with no user, listing or disbursement figure published](2026-01-27-proxigab-national-digital-platform-smes-techafricanews).

The funding it exists to match is thin. An annual tracker records [two funded startups raising US$300,000 in calendar 2025, of which US$100,000 was artificial intelligence, 0.2% of the African total](2026-02-03-disrupt-africa-african-tech-startups-funding-report-2025) - a self-declared minimum floor counted by funded venture, and not commensurable with other trackers. No prior-year Cameroonian figure on the same basis is held.

summary: A [smart campus and learning platform for training public agents went to stakeholder discussion on 20 August 2026](2026-08-20-globalinfosnews-smart-campus-minfopra-koica).
developments:
2026-08-20 - a [smart campus and learning-management platform for training public agents went to stakeholder discussion between the public service ministry and a donor partner](2026-08-20-globalinfosnews-smart-campus-minfopra-koica).

No launch date, cohort size, budget or platform specification is published, and nothing states how it relates to the local-government baseline recorded elsewhere in this report, on which most decentralised authorities employ no digitally trained staff. It is the only civil-service digital training instrument the base holds for the window.

summary: The [2025 artificial-intelligence challenge trained 100 young people across five cities](2025-07-23-leconomie-snk-ia-challenge-2025); no 2026 edition or outcome figure is held.
developments:
2025-06-16 to 2025-07-18 - the challenge [trained 100 young Cameroonians at strict gender parity, twenty per city across five cities](2025-07-23-leconomie-snk-ia-challenge-2025). It is privately funded.

No 2026 edition, follow-up or outcome figure is held, so continuation is unestablished rather than discontinued. Nothing else on this ledger measures digital literacy in the general population: there is no survey, no index reading and no national skills figure at either end of the window.

summary: The [secondary-education ministry formally adopted generated simulations for classroom use on 17 August 2026](2026-08-19-dba-minesec-simulation-ia-e-education).
developments:
2026-08-17 - the ministry [formally adopted artificial-intelligence-generated simulations for use in secondary schools, with teacher demonstrations in chemistry, biology, languages and industrial techniques](2026-08-19-dba-minesec-simulation-ia-e-education).

It is an adoption decision, not a delivered programme: no teacher-training plan, curriculum change, device provision or distribution mechanism to schools without connectivity is published, and no pedagogical evaluation or accuracy check has been carried out on the material. Nothing else in the window touches technology teaching in secondary schools.

summary: A [chair in digital governance was created at a Yaounde university](2026-02-11-university-yaounde-ii-art-digital-governance-chair-techafricanews), and [115 internships opened across all ten regions](2026-07-22-camtel-minesup-115-internships).
developments:
2026-02-11 - a partnership formalised after four years of negotiation [created a chair to structure research and training, fund doctoral study and advanced training for regulator staff, governed by a scientific steering committee](2026-02-11-university-yaounde-ii-art-digital-governance-chair-techafricanews). No funding figure, chair-holder, intake or start date is published.

2026-06-03 - a [memorandum between the state operator and the higher-education ministry was signed](2026-06-04-camtel-minesup-youth-skills-telecoms-techafricanews), and a [first implementation wave recruited 115 internships across all ten regions, in disciplines from telecommunications and cybersecurity to finance and law](2026-07-22-camtel-minesup-115-internships); no stipend, duration or conversion-to-employment figure is published.

summary: The [60,000-specialists-by-2040 target has no enrolment, graduation or expenditure figure against it](2026-07-31-cameroon-pm-national-ai-strategy-completion) at either end of the window.
developments:
The target was set out in July 2025: [60,000 specialists by 2040 including 40% women, 12,000 direct jobs, and 0.8 to 1.2% of GDP](2025-07-10-snia-60000-ai-experts-by-2040-wearetech).

2026-07-30 - the [strategy carrying it was still being developed a year on, with modules in curricula named among ten priorities and a roadmap tabled but no adoption, budget line or trainee count](2026-07-31-cameroon-pm-national-ai-strategy-completion). No enrolment, graduation or expenditure figure exists against the target at either end.

What is measured is small and private: [481 young people trained and 50 international certifications issued across an operator's six digital centres](2026-05-10-orange-cameroon-sixth-digital-center-maroua-techreviewafrica), on the company's own unaudited figures.

summary: A [EUR 3m gender-divide project remains active with no dated progress, output or Cameroon-side figure recorded in the window](2023-01-01-bmz-cmr-002-bridging-the-digital-gender-divide).
developments:
The project is [recorded active with EUR 3m committed for 2023 to 2026](2023-01-01-bmz-cmr-002-bridging-the-digital-gender-divide), and the position is identical at both ends of the window: no dated progress, output or Cameroon-side figure.

It is the only finance record in the tracked non-state set classified to any inclusion subject. The base holds no sex-disaggregated access, usage or ownership figure for Cameroon at all, so a project running to 2026 on closing a gender divide has no measurement of that divide to be read against.

progress: Movement, on a tender with no award held, against a universal-service fund abolished before the window
summary: A [FCFA 55bn rural component targeting 328 unserved localities by 2028 went to tender](2025-11-09 Cameroon aims to connect 328 rural communities by 2028 (PATNUC)), with no award on file.
developments:
2025-11-09 - a limited national tender opened for the rural component of the national connectivity project: [FCFA 55bn, 328 unserved localities targeted by 2028 in two phases of 120 sites plus an optional 208, with works expected by 30 December 2026](2025-11-09 Cameroon aims to connect 328 rural communities by 2028 (PATNUC)). No award, contract or site count is held after the tender opened.

The domestic mechanism that would otherwise fund this is gone: the [Special Telecommunications Development Fund stays abolished and universal-service money is not separately traceable in FY2024, FY2025 or FY2026](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-45-451), so rural connectivity now runs through donor projects rather than a domestic account.

progress: Movement, the enumeration close slipped to 15 September 2026
summary: The [fourth population and agriculture census is still in the field](2026-08-03-cameroon-population-census-extended-by-45-days), on a complementary period running to 15 September 2026.
developments:
The last census was in 2005; a pilot ran October to November 2025, and [enumeration used smartphones combined with satellite imagery and sample estimation for areas inaccessible through insecurity or isolation](2026-03-11-leconomie-census-2026-digital-satellite-data-collection) - the only satellite-data item the base carries for this country.

2026-07-31 - an order made public [extended the field work: a complementary period runs from 1 August to 15 September 2026 to complete identification of households, persons and agricultural holdings missed by the 29 May close, enumeration having run with 32,059 agents at a budget of FCFA 13.28bn against FCFA 64bn initially projected, with no results published](2026-08-03-cameroon-population-census-extended-by-45-days).

progress: Mixed, a development-goal indicator platform launched while the national open-data policy stayed unpublished
summary: An [indicator platform launched on 17 September 2025](2025-09-19-leconomie-open-sdg-platform-sdg-monitoring), while the [open-data policy provided for in the roadmap is still unpublished](2025-07-08-snia-2040-ai-roadmap-seven-pillars-techafricanews).
developments:
2025-09-17 - the statistics institute [launched a platform publishing development-goal indicator data for public access, built in 2024 with configuration work through the first half of 2025](2025-09-19-leconomie-open-sdg-platform-sdg-monitoring). No update cadence, indicator count or usage figure is on file, so whether it is being maintained is unestablished.

The policy layer did not move: a national open-data policy is [provided for in the artificial-intelligence roadmap with nothing published](2025-07-08-snia-2040-ai-roadmap-seven-pillars-techafricanews), and it is [not among the ten priority areas tabled to cabinet on 30 July 2026](2026-07-31-cameroon-pm-national-ai-strategy-completion). No licence, catalogue or publication obligation exists behind the one platform that does publish.

summary: The state operator [held a working session with a hyperscaler's Africa executives and the US embassy ICT representative](2026-07-24-cameroon-camtel-aws-cloud-ai-partnership); talks only.
developments:
2026-07 - the state operator [approached a United States hyperscaler, with a working session involving its Africa executives and the US embassy's information technology representative](2026-07-24-cameroon-camtel-aws-cloud-ai-partnership), [reported earlier the same month as digital transformation talks](2026-07-08-camtel-aws-digital-transformation-talks-techafricanews).

There is no agreement, investment commitment or timeline, and no answer on where Cameroonian data would sit. That last point matters here: the approach sits against the same operator's own sovereign-cloud line and against the regional data-residency recommendation its regulator's peers adopted in February 2026.
