summary: A [fourth video-surveillance tranche of FCFA 39.2bn was authorised](2025-12-23-lejour-urban-videosurveillance-loan) and a [fibre phase of about FCFA 108.4bn was authorised for signature](2026-03-11-leconomie-china-eximbank-fibre-backbone-phase4-loan).
developments:
2025-12-17 - a decree [authorised a fourth video-surveillance loan of FCFA 39.2bn, bringing FCFA 150.8bn mobilised over eight years across three Chinese lenders](2025-12-23-lejour-urban-videosurveillance-loan); the [first phase, borrowed by the defence ministry, delivered 1,500 cameras and 2,000 portable radios](2026-07-22-aiddata-58535-bank-of-china-cameroon-video-surveillance-phase1) on accounts that disagree about amounts and dates.

2026-03-06 - a decree [authorised signature of CNY 1,350,963,161, about FCFA 108.4bn, for a further 4,000 km of backbone, a national data centre and regional links to Chad, the Central African Republic and Nigeria](2026-03-11-leconomie-china-eximbank-fibre-backbone-phase4-loan). The loan is not confirmed signed and the executing contractor is not confirmed.

summary: The EU signed a [FCFA 9.83bn grant for digital SME competitiveness in June 2026](2026-06-16-european-union-cmr-2026-acceleration-numerique-cameroun).
developments:
[The European Union signed a grant convention of FCFA 9,830,000,000 with Cameroon to strengthen the digital competitiveness of very small, small and medium enterprises, one of three financing conventions signed the same day at the Cameroon-EU Economic Forum](2026-06-16-european-union-cmr-2026-acceleration-numerique-cameroun). [Further EU grants covering digital, cocoa and forests followed](2026-06-17-cameroon-tribune-eu-grants-digital-cocoa-forests).

[The EU's Multiannual Indicative Programme for 2021 to 2027 names digitalisation of administrative procedures and generalised access to dematerialised information as a governance-efficiency objective](2022-01-01-eu-mip-2021-2027-cameroun).

No Global Gateway country package for Cameroon and no delegation statement on data adequacy is held.

progress: No change, one valued instrument and it is nineteen years old
summary: India committed [FCFA 1.4bn under the Pan-African e-Network country accord of 3 September 2007](2007-09-03-india-exim-bank-cmr-2007-cameroon-pan-african-enetwork).
developments:
[The Pan-African e-Network country accord was signed on 3 September 2007 by Cameroon's Minister of External Relations, against a commitment from the Government of India of FCFA 1,400,000,000 covering network implementation, recurring costs and five years' maintenance](2007-09-03-india-exim-bank-cmr-2007-cameroon-pan-african-enetwork). [India's Commerce and Industry Minister named digital technologies among areas for expanded cooperation when he met the Prime Minister at WTO MC14 in Yaounde on 26 March 2026, and invited Cameroon to the India-Africa Conference](2026-03-27-cameroon-tribune-goyal-ngute-digital-technologies).

The 2026 contact is an expression of interest and not an instrument. Nothing reports what the e-Network delivered or whether it still runs.

summary: The 2016 plan [expired and a successor has been in preparation since 5 August 2024](2025-02-08-patnuc-plan-cameroun-numerique-2020-expire-nouvelle-strategie); what stands in its place is a [ministerial roadmap for 2026](2026-02-24-digitalbusiness-feuille-de-route-numerique-2026-cameroun).
developments:
The project unit's own statement is the finding: the [2016 national digital plan's five-year validity has expired and a successor aligned to the national development strategy has been under preparation since 5 August 2024](2025-02-08-patnuc-plan-cameroun-numerique-2020-expire-nouvelle-strategie). Eighteen months on, no draft, adoption instrument or date is published.

2026-02-19 - the minister set out a [2026 digital transformation roadmap tied to the national development strategy and the head of state's end-of-year message, covering artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and electronic government](2026-02-24-digitalbusiness-feuille-de-route-numerique-2026-cameroun). An annual address is not a strategy.

Where planning is being bought rather than written, it is narrow: a [six-month assignment to produce a master plan for digitising the public-procurement information system went to a consulting grouping for FCFA 241.36 million](2026-09-02-cmr-camerounlink-plan-directeur-numerisation-marches-publics).

summary: The only broadband strategy is the [2016 plan, whose first strategic axis was broadband infrastructure and whose validity expired](2016-01-01-minpostel-plan-strategique-cameroun-numerique-2020); procurement runs without one, [362 rural localities out to tender](2025-11-12-armp-appel-offres-connectivite-haut-debit-zones-rurales-patnuc).
developments:
The instrument is a decade old and lapsed: the ministry's own page [makes broadband infrastructure development the plan's first strategic axis](2016-01-01-minpostel-plan-strategique-cameroun-numerique-2020), and its five-year validity has [expired with the successor still in preparation](2025-02-08-patnuc-plan-cameroun-numerique-2020-expire-nouvelle-strategie).

2025-11-06 - the delivery is proceeding anyway. An internationally competitive tender covers [supply, installation and commissioning of mobile broadband equipment across 362 rural localities in two tranches, financed by a World Bank credit](2025-11-12-armp-appel-offres-connectivite-haut-debit-zones-rurales-patnuc).

2025-10-03 - a companion notice seeks a consultant to [survey existing provision and specify bandwidth for connecting public entities, naming rural local authorities, hospitals, primary schools, secondary and teacher-training schools, vocational centres, women and family promotion centres and centres for disadvantaged persons](2025-10-03-armp-patnuc-connectivite-entites-publiques-ami).

Neither is a strategy: both are components of one financed project, and no national target, coverage figure or timetable sits above them.

summary: Two draft bills were [technically validated at a national workshop of 3 to 14 November 2025, with interoperability, digital identification and data-protection recommendations integrated](2025-11-19-patnuc-atelier-ebolowa-2025-reformes-numeriques). Neither is enacted.
developments:
The workshop [validated a bill on electronic government and access to public information and a second on electronic commerce and electronic transactions, integrating interoperability, digital identification and data-protection recommendations, with the drafts left pending ministerial and institutional finalisation](2025-11-19-patnuc-atelier-ebolowa-2025-reformes-numeriques).

The first was [officially validated after that workshop, establishing proactive publication of public information](2026-01-21-dmf-cameroun-loi-egov-acces-information-publique-validation-officielle) and remains unenacted.

Meanwhile the exchange layer is being assigned by instruction rather than statute: the telecommunications ministry [tasked the state operator with carrying national data and infrastructure interoperability, with no design, timetable or budget published](2026-08-18-dba-fgi-cameroun-camtel-interoperabilite-nationale).

summary: The regulator counts [more than 31.5 million active mobile subscriptions in 2024](2025-08-12-art-observatoire-annuel-2024-marche-communications-electroniques); one operator claims [13.09 million customers and 54.3 per cent share for 2025](2026-03-17-ecomatin-mtn-cameroon-revenus-2025-base-clients), unconfirmed by the regulator.
developments:
The regulator's annual observatory records [more than 31.5 million active mobile subscriptions, mobile revenue up nearly 12 per cent at FCFA 631 billion, falling voice traffic and a marked drop in text messaging as users migrate to messaging applications, and more than 4,700 passive infrastructure sites](2025-08-12-art-observatoire-annuel-2024-marche-communications-electroniques). It also names its own limit: incomplete data from some operators weakens sector monitoring.

2026-03-17 - one operator's group accounts claim [13.09 million customers against 11.87 million a year earlier, a 54.3 per cent market share the regulator has not confirmed, mobile penetration of 80.7 per cent of the population, revenue of FCFA 437.26 billion up 19.4 per cent and capital spending of FCFA 206.72 billion up about 39 per cent](2026-03-17-ecomatin-mtn-cameroon-revenus-2025-base-clients).

Subscriptions are not users: the same observatory counts [over 15 million internet subscriptions, 99 per cent of them mobile](2025-12-09-art-2024-annual-observatory-telecom-market-techafricanews), and no unique-user or population-penetration series is published by the regulator itself.

summary: The regulator [publishes compared tariffs and regulates wholesale rather than retail prices](2024-04-12-art-tarifs-compares-operateurs-premier-semestre-2023); handset cost moved instead, through [duty by device identifier](2026-04-01-imei-system-mobile-device-import-duties-camcis-techcabal) and [network blocking from 1 September 2026](2026-08-24-cameroun-telephones-non-dedouanes-1er-septembre).
developments:
The regulator's stated position is that [in a structurally oligopolistic sector, regulation targets the wholesale market between operators to make cost components objective, fair, non-discriminatory and transparent](2024-04-12-art-tarifs-compares-operateurs-premier-semestre-2023) — not retail prices. Its own observatory records that [retail tariffs remain rigid despite falling interconnection costs](2025-08-12-art-observatoire-annuel-2024-marche-communications-electroniques), and the most recent published comparison is for the first half of 2023.

What has changed is the cost of the handset. From 1 April 2026 [importers must declare each device by its identifier through the customs platform and pay duties before network use, with an amnesty for devices already connected](2026-04-01-imei-system-mobile-device-import-duties-camcis-techcabal), the finance ministry stating the reform adds no new tax and automates an existing one.

2026-09-01 - [deactivation of handsets on which duty has not been paid begins, under a communique signed by the finance minister on 20 August 2026](2026-08-24-cameroun-telephones-non-dedouanes-1er-septembre). No affordability basket, price index or income-share figure is published against any of it.

summary: One public body [put a two-site virtual infrastructure and recovery upgrade to tender in December 2025](2025-12-19-armp-src-datacenter-upgrade-tender); ministries otherwise [host inside the state operator's single facility](2022-06-15-minfopra-camtel-convention-partenariat).
developments:
2025-12-19 - the state debt recovery company opened an [upgrade of its virtual infrastructure and standardisation of its data centre across sites at Yaounde and Douala, buying virtualisation and live-recovery licences at both, spare disks and power and cabling components, at an estimated FCFA 40,000,000 including tax](2025-12-19-armp-src-datacenter-upgrade-tender). It is the only two-site recovery arrangement the base holds for any public body, and it is at tender rather than in service.

The prevailing pattern is single-site hosting with the state operator. A convention of 13 June 2022 [puts the public service ministry's server in the operator's data centre with 50 Mbit/s to central services and 4 Mbit/s to deconcentrated services](2022-06-15-minfopra-camtel-convention-partenariat), and in January 2026 the examination board agreed to [host national examination data in the same facility](2026-01-15-camtel-obc-baccalaureate-framework-agreement), which is [tier-certified and tourable](2026-08-14-cameroon-camtel-zamengoe-data-centre).

No replication, backup or recovery arrangement between that facility and any other is stated, and no national consolidation policy exists.

summary: A [single gas plant's maintenance shutdown from 5 to 7 August 2026 cut southern grid capacity and disrupted supply](2026-08-05-minee-kribi-centrale-gaz-maintenance-perturbations). No data centre's supply arrangement is published.
developments:
2026-08-05 - the energy ministry announced that the gas-fired thermal plant at Kribi would be [shut down for the whole duration of pipeline terminal maintenance from 5 to 7 August 2026, temporarily reducing the generation capacity of the southern interconnected grid and disrupting supply in some localities, with all other available generation mobilised to limit the effect](2026-08-05-minee-kribi-centrale-gaz-maintenance-perturbations). It is the clearest dated statement of how one plant's outage propagates to the grid the country's data centres sit on.

The facilities themselves are being built against that grid. The minister toured a [privately built data centre in the port zone of Douala in July 2025, its promoter describing it as one of the most advanced in the country and stating it already hosts data for several public and private bodies](2025-07-14-minpostel-st-digital-data-center-visite), and a separate operator has [confirmed US$75m for a Douala data centre designed in part for artificial-intelligence workloads with dedicated power](2026-08-29-cameroon-cybastion-douala-ai-data-centre).

No data-centre power supply arrangement, energy efficiency standard, tariff or water requirement is published for any of them.

progress: No change, a standing position the base holds for the first time
summary: The only national household instrument is the [first national survey on access to energy, water and sanitation](2022-12-01-ins-minee-enace1-household-access-energy-water-sanitation), whose access figures sit past the capture limit.
developments:
The statistics institute conducted the survey for the water and energy ministry, its [household component reporting on access to electricity](2022-12-01-ins-minee-enace1-household-access-energy-water-sanitation). The capture reaches the access-to-electricity section before the fetch limit, so the base holds the instrument and not the figures in it.

No rural electrification programme, target, connection count or urban and rural split is published at any date, which is what makes the telecommunications side unreadable: [power is a stated constraint on rural sites](2026-08-05-minee-kribi-centrale-gaz-maintenance-perturbations) with nothing measuring it.

summary: Government systems run on one state operator's estate: [ministry servers and bandwidth since 2022](2022-06-15-minfopra-camtel-convention-partenariat), [900 sites and a secure data centre agreed in September 2025](2025-09-18-camtel-mintoul-tourism-digital-partnership), [examination data from January 2026](2026-01-15-camtel-obc-baccalaureate-framework-agreement).
developments:
The concentration is the finding. A 2022 convention [puts the public service ministry's server in the operator's data centre and supplies its bandwidth](2022-06-15-minfopra-camtel-convention-partenariat). In September 2025 the operator agreed with the tourism ministry to [connect more than 900 tourism and administrative sites by fibre and to provide a secure data centre](2025-09-18-camtel-mintoul-tourism-digital-partnership). In January 2026 it agreed with the examination board to [host national examination data in its tier-certified facility under a sovereign national cloud framing](2026-01-15-camtel-obc-baccalaureate-framework-agreement).

The most systematic assessment of what sits underneath remains a [financier's country diagnostic of 2020](2020-06-01-worldbank-cameroon-digital-economy-assessment), six years old.

No inventory of state systems, no uptime or availability figure, no refresh cycle and no continuity arrangement for the single facility most of this depends on is published.

summary: Training for public agents is [at consultant selection, results published 28 April 2026](2026-04-28-armp-patnuc-elearning-consultant-selection), alongside a [smart campus under discussion with a donor](2026-08-20-globalinfosnews-smart-campus-minfopra-koica).
developments:
2026-04-28 - the digital transformation project published the results of its expression-of-interest process for a [consultant to deliver digital transformation training and capacity building for public agents through an electronic learning platform](2026-04-28-armp-patnuc-elearning-consultant-selection). No platform, curriculum, cohort or budget is published, and the project itself was [restructured in 2025](2025-09-01-worldbank-patnuc-restructuring-paper).

2026-08 - the public service ministry and a donor partner are [discussing a smart campus and learning-management platform for training public agents](2026-08-20-globalinfosnews-smart-campus-minfopra-koica).

Two training vehicles at procurement and discussion stage is the whole of the capacity story the base holds. No count of technical staff in the administration, no vacancy rate and no skills assessment is published.

summary: An [integrated sectoral education management information platform was launched on 13 May 2025](2025-05-13-unesco-cameroon-integrated-emis-platform-launch) with no coverage or data-flow detail published.
developments:
2025-05-13 - the education agency of the United Nations, the government and a financier [officially launched an integrated sectoral platform for the education management information system together with its methodological tools](2025-05-13-unesco-cameroon-integrated-emis-platform-launch). The launch notice carries no coverage, participating-ministry or data-flow detail, so what the base holds is that an integrated platform exists and not what it integrates.

The work under it is being bought separately: [EUR 8m of technical assistance over 36 months covers the education management information system, the basic-education ministry's mapping platform, interconnection of the education databases and dynamic reporting](2026-07-31-cameroon-unesco-basic-education-agreement-websig-database-interconnection).

The examinations leg is being wired to a different place again: [three pillars agreed — site interconnection, examination data in the sovereign national cloud, and examination-management platforms](2026-01-19-camtel-baccalaureate-office-digitize-national-exams-techafricanews), with nothing reported live.

summary: The [adaptive safety nets project took additional financing in August 2025](2025-08-18-worldbank-asneip-additional-financing-project-paper); the unified social register it feeds is [equipping 100 pilot social centres](2024-08-28-yaounde-govt-launches-programme-to-register-socially-vulnerable-persons).
developments:
The register is the object any interoperability would run through: its registration programme [was launched on 23 August 2024, equipping 100 pilot social centres across the ten regions with a computer, printer, modem and internet subscription](2024-08-28-yaounde-govt-launches-programme-to-register-socially-vulnerable-persons).

2025-08-18 - a financier's project paper [proposes an additional credit for the adaptive safety nets and economic inclusion project](2025-08-18-worldbank-asneip-additional-financing-project-paper), the operation that carries beneficiary identification and payment. The capture is truncated part-way through the first component, so what it provides for on interoperability is not established from it.

Nothing states that the register exchanges data with the identity system, the payroll system or any sectoral database. The country's participation in a [twenty-one-country programme on inclusive digital social protection](2025-10-27-across-21-countries-shared-journey-inclusive-digital-social-protection) is the nearest thing to a stated ambition for it.

summary: The social insurance fund paid [FCFA 6.46bn to 49,132 parents for 119,664 children principally by mobile money from 5 October 2025](2025-10-24-cnps-special-school-grants-mobile-money) — the largest government-to-person disbursement the base holds with a stated digital channel.
developments:
The enabling instrument is a [2022 decree establishing the general framework for financial operations of the State and other public entities by electronic means](2022-09-16-decree-2022-8001-electronic-state-financial-operations); the captured text is a scan truncated near section 23.

2025-10-05 - the fund [disbursed more than FCFA 6.4 billion under a special school reopening allowance, FCFA 54,000 a child, reaching 49,132 insured parents for 119,664 children, paid principally by mobile money, with school certificates submitted and verified digitally to prevent fraud](2025-10-24-cnps-special-school-grants-mobile-money). Its director general describes it as a first in the history of the social security system, funded from the fund's own surplus.

The inbound leg is mandatory where the outbound is not: an order of 28 May 2025 [makes the treasury's platform the only lawful channel for collecting non-tax revenue](2025-06-05-cameroon-mandates-digital-payment-platform-non-tax-revenues). No equivalent rule, volume or digital share exists for payments out.

summary: There is no population register: the census is [still in the field, its enumeration extended by order of 30 July 2026 to 15 September](2026-07-30-order-111-cab-pm-rgph4-additional-census-period), and the register in production is the [electoral one at about 8.2 million](2025-09-11-cameroon-signals-urgency-biometric-voter-id-collection).
developments:
2026-07-30 - an order [set an additional collection period for the joint enumeration operations of the fourth population and housing census and the core module of the agriculture and livestock census](2026-07-30-order-111-cab-pm-rgph4-additional-census-period). The complementary period [runs to 15 September 2026 to complete identification of households, persons and holdings missed by the May close](2026-08-03-cameroon-population-census-extended-by-45-days). A census in the field is not a register.

The only person-level register in production is electoral: [about 8.2 million voters under deduplication ahead of the October 2025 presidential vote, with more than 350,000 biometric cards uncollected in one region alone](2025-09-11-cameroon-signals-urgency-biometric-voter-id-collection).

The civil registration programme that would underpin a population register has [an implementation partner engaged and a 2029 target, to integrate with the biometric identity card and the voter kits](2026-01-12-councils-begin-issuance-digital-birth-certificates-biometricupdate).

summary: The commercial register's computerisation covers [30 sites, equipped and trained by April 2024 and awaiting handover to the State](2024-04-03-ohada-informatisation-rccm-cameroun-point-etape); tax registration moved to a [new application mandatory from 1 July 2026](2026-07-16-lefisk-atom-dgi-immatriculation-fiscale-guide).
developments:
2024-04-02 - a quadripartite review recorded that the programme financed by a French development agency had [acquired equipment for all 30 sites, court registries and training centres, carried out electrical and network works and standards upgrades, and trained administrators and users on the register management software, with the remaining sites to be finished in the following weeks ahead of official handover to the State](2024-04-03-ohada-informatisation-rccm-cameroun-point-etape). No handover, register size or filing volume is recorded since.

Registration of businesses for tax purposes changed hands in 2026: a finance ministry communique of 10 April 2026 announced [a new registration application replacing the previous platform, the old one closing on 30 June 2026, the new one mandatory from 1 July 2026, a registration fee of FCFA 1,000, and existing taxpayers given until 31 December 2026 to re-register](2026-07-16-lefisk-atom-dgi-immatriculation-fiscale-guide).

The one volume figure the base holds for business registration is external: [more than 25,000 small and medium enterprises registered through an international agency's platform](2020-12-07-unctad-platform-powers-registration-of-over-25000-businesses-in-cameroon).

summary: Registration moved to a [new application mandatory from 1 July 2026, with re-registration required by 31 December](2026-07-16-lefisk-atom-dgi-immatriculation-fiscale-guide), over a base of [400,000 registered taxpayers in 2024](2025-07-11-recettes-fiscales-contribution-des-particuliers-historiquement-faible).
developments:
The base is thin and growing: [400,000 registered taxpayers in 2024, a fivefold rise in a decade, with individuals contributing a historically low 7 per cent of tax receipts before 2024 against 17 per cent in comparable economies](2025-07-11-recettes-fiscales-contribution-des-particuliers-historiquement-faible).

2026-07-01 - the registration front end was replaced: [the old platform closed on 30 June 2026, the new application became mandatory from 1 July, registration carries a fee of FCFA 1,000, and existing taxpayers have until 31 December 2026 to re-register](2026-07-16-lefisk-atom-dgi-immatriculation-fiscale-guide). A compulsory re-registration is the sharpest test of a register's quality, and no result from it is published.

The core system behind it is also being replaced: an [integrated tax and duty management system was contracted on 10 April 2026 to a four-firm consortium at EUR 5.997m excluding tax](2026-05-13-leconomie-tax-digitalisation-dgi), and the tax directorate's own [2026-2028 strategic plan](2026-01-01-dgt-strategic-plan-2026-2028) sits over both.

summary: The system is [housed within a project implementation unit and stated to be extendable to other programmes](2023-08-16-worldbank-cameroon-social-safety-nets-icr); take-up of the register over it is uneven — [55,097 people across eight communes in one region](2026-04-15-cameroon-tribune-resuc-ouest-sensibilises).
developments:
The completion report records a [management information system developed and housed within the project implementation unit and stated to be extendable to other safety-net programmes, alongside capacity building for the statistics institute and the census bureau](2023-08-16-worldbank-cameroon-social-safety-nets-icr). A system inside a project unit is a system with an end date.

2026-04-08 - the social affairs minister toured one region because [only 55,097 socially vulnerable people across eight communes were registered, which the ministry attributes to weak take-up](2026-04-15-cameroon-tribune-resuc-ouest-sensibilises). A ministry seminar in September 2025 was [devoted to popularising the register](2025-09-18-nkolandom-minas-resuc-seminaire).

The registration infrastructure exists: [100 pilot social centres across the ten regions equipped with a computer, printer, modem and internet subscription](2024-08-28-yaounde-govt-launches-programme-to-register-socially-vulnerable-persons). No national coverage figure against the vulnerable population is published.

summary: Three procurement steps in five months and no system: a [private project manager sought in March](2026-03-16-armp-ami-digitalisation-domaniale-cadastrale-fonciere-sif), a [geolocation contract awarded in May](2026-05-11-mindcaf-attribution-geolocalisation-proprietes-wouri), and a [revenue-digitisation feasibility study tendered in August](2026-08-17-mindcaf-appel-offres-modernisation-digitalisation-recettes-domaniales).
developments:
2026-03-16 - the housing ministry sought a [private project manager for digitisation of land, cadastral, property and patrimonial services, procedures and products](2026-03-16-armp-ami-digitalisation-domaniale-cadastrale-fonciere-sif).

2026-05-11 - the lands ministry awarded a national firm [FCFA 12,509,325 over four months to operationalise geolocation of administrative properties in one department](2026-05-11-mindcaf-attribution-geolocalisation-proprietes-wouri).

2026-08-17 - the same ministry opened an [urgent-procedure tender for a technical, organisational, institutional and financial feasibility study toward modernising and digitising the management of land, cadastral and property revenue, financed from its own 2026 investment budget](2026-08-17-mindcaf-appel-offres-modernisation-digitalisation-recettes-domaniales).

Behind them sits a [2025 memorandum with a domestic firm to digitise land-tenure procedures starting in one division](2025-08-26-digitising-mindcaf-procedures-modernising-land-tenure-cameroon) and a [Douala programme to digitise about 200,000 land files with a digital possession certificate, with no budget, timeline or start date published](2026-05-07-leconomie-douala-digital-land-registry-possession-certificate). The ministry's own cadastre modernisation appropriation meanwhile [fell 44.2 per cent for FY2026](2025-11-26-cmr-2026-37-380).

summary: One-stop shops for land-use and construction permits were [instituted in urban communities by decree in 2018](2018-12-10-decret-2018-9704-guichet-unique-communautes-urbaines); [230 councils, about 64 per cent, are supported by the technology agency](2026-07-16-antic-urges-north-west-councils-digital-transformation-techafricanews).
developments:
The 2018 decree [institutes one-stop shops in urban communities to facilitate issue of administrative acts relating to land use and construction](2018-12-10-decret-2018-9704-guichet-unique-communautes-urbaines). The captured text covers the definitions and missions; the articles on fees, sanctions and transitional provisions were not captured, and no count of shops opened or acts issued is published.

The coverage figures that exist are the technology agency's: [230 councils, about 64 per cent nationally, supported by the agency, 48.6 per cent of North West councils operating functional websites, 335 municipal portals developed and 145 authorities equipped](2026-07-16-antic-urges-north-west-councils-digital-transformation-techafricanews).

2025-09-11 - the municipal digitalisation programme presented [phase-one deliverables covering site and portal infrastructure for communes](2025-09-14-centrifuge-hebdo-digitalisation-communes-cvuc), and a separate [FCFA 92bn local-government digitisation programme is announced with no financier, signed instrument or start date](2026-06-04-digi-cor-163m-digitize-local-governments-wearetech).

summary: Two donor and diaspora initiatives rather than a state programme: [health staff at four integrated centres trained on mobile health software](2025-10-06-mkwbc-mhealth-southern-region-health-centres) and an [eighteen-month rural telehealth project from September 2025](2025-09-01-smartmobileclinic-telehealth-rural-communities-cameroon).
developments:
2025-10-06 - health personnel at four named integrated health centres in one region were [trained in the use of mobile health software over workshops running to 11 October](2025-10-06-mkwbc-mhealth-southern-region-health-centres).

2025-09 - a diaspora-backed project began an [eighteen-month effort to expand telehealth services in rural communities](2025-09-01-smartmobileclinic-telehealth-rural-communities-cameroon).

Neither states a patient volume, a facility count beyond the four, or an integration with the national health information system.

The state's own instrument is broader and newer: [deployment beginning across ten regions, 175 health districts and 395 facilities, replacing paper forms, with over 1,500 health workers to be trained](2026-08-07-cameroon-scanform-smartphones-health-data). Nothing states how many of those 395 facilities are rural.

summary: The basic-education policy rests on a survey of [852 schools of which 29.92 per cent were rural and 417 were not connected](2022-01-01-minedub-politique-tic-cadre-strategique-education-de-base); primary schools are [named among the targets of a connectivity study](2025-10-03-armp-patnuc-connectivite-entites-publiques-ami).
developments:
The policy is the standing instrument and the survey behind it is the only measurement: [852 schools including 29.92 per cent rural and 417 not connected](2022-01-01-minedub-politique-tic-cadre-strategique-education-de-base). The capture covers its front matter only, so the measures it sets are not held, and no later coverage or connection figure is published against it.

2025-10-03 - primary schools are [named among the public entities a consultant is to survey and specify bandwidth for, alongside rural local authorities, hospitals, secondary and teacher-training schools, vocational centres and social centres](2025-10-03-armp-patnuc-connectivite-entites-publiques-ami). That is a study, not a connection.

Four years after the policy, nothing states how many primary schools have power, a device or a connection.

summary: The social insurance fund [described biometric identification, automated pension-file processing, automated customer response and an electronic wallet already running inside it](2026-02-17-digitalbusiness-africa-minpostel-atelier-ia-administrations) — the only deployed use the base holds.
developments:
2026-02-17 - at a telecommunications ministry workshop for public administrations, the fund's director general [set out artificial intelligence already deployed inside the institution: biometric identification, automated pension-file processing, automated customer response and an electronic wallet](2026-02-17-digitalbusiness-africa-minpostel-atelier-ia-administrations). It is a self-description at a workshop, with no evaluation, model or error rate published.

2025-07 - a government artificial-intelligence showcase was [presented at a public administration trade fair](2025-07-09-dgb-gov-ai-cenadi-intelligence-artificielle-gouvernementale).

2026-07-17 - the public service ministry and a North African counterpart [explored use cases for automating repetitive tasks and reducing processing times for pensions and reclassifications through the biometric payroll system](2026-07-17-minfopra-cooperation-cameroun-maroc-ia-administration): stated intent, no implementation date or instrument.

The strategy that would govern any of it is [still in drafting a year on, with ten priority areas attached and no adoption instrument published](2026-07-31-cameroon-pm-national-ai-strategy-completion), and the payroll system it would run through [flagged more than 53,000 fraudulent claims by June 2026](2026-08-10-cameroon-fake-birth-certificates-payroll-fraud-census).

summary: A [civil-society initiative launched on 9 July 2026 addresses deepfakes and voice cloning alongside other cybercrime](2026-07-10-stopblablacam-digital-shield-cybercrime-victims). No rule on synthetic media exists.
developments:
2026-07-09 - three foundations launched an initiative to [help victims of cybercrime speak out, addressing deepfakes and artificial-intelligence voice cloning specifically alongside other cybercrime, with a telecommunications ministry representative attending](2026-07-10-stopblablacam-digital-shield-cybercrime-victims). It is civil-society-led and carries no legal instrument.

There is nothing above it. No rule on synthetic media, no takedown route and no prosecution is on the record; an [artificial-intelligence authority and presidential council are still not created and absent from the strategy's ten priority areas, which carry only adaptation of the legal framework](2026-07-31-cameroon-government-engages-on-harnessing-ai).

The general data-protection statute is [in force with no supervisory authority operating](2024-12-23-cmr-loi-2024-017-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel), which leaves no regulator to apply it to generated content.

summary: Two independent institutes publish on digital policy — a [2026 brief turning the artificial intelligence strategy into an implementation agenda](2026-01-06-nkafu-ai-future-of-work-cameroon) and a [December 2025 review of technology-sector law and readiness](2025-12-08-camepi-economic-freedom-through-technology).
developments:
One institute issued a [note in November 2022 analysing digitalisation and the performance of public administrations](2022-11-09-nkafu-digitalization-performance-public-administrations), and a [brief in January 2026 translating the national artificial intelligence strategy into an implementation agenda covering infrastructure and energy, skills, governance and inclusion of the informal sector](2026-01-06-nkafu-ai-future-of-work-cameroon).

Another published in December 2025 a [review of technology-sector law, the digital transformation project, the artificial intelligence strategy and readiness indicators, with policy recommendations](2025-12-08-camepi-economic-freedom-through-technology).

Neither is commissioned by government and no research funding line is held. The academic side is newer and narrower: a [chair in digital governance is being set up to structure research and training, fund doctoral study and provide advanced training for regulator staff](2026-02-11-university-yaounde-ii-art-digital-governance-chair-techafricanews).

progress: No change, a standing position the base holds for the first time
summary: The one feedback channel is a [public conciliator's online complaint form covering two regions](2025-01-01-opicswr-make-a-complaint-portal). No nationwide portal exists.
developments:
The office of the public independent conciliator, created under the local authorities code and a 2020 decree and [covering two regions only, runs an online complaint intake form](2025-01-01-opicswr-make-a-complaint-portal). No complaint volume, response duty or resolution figure is published.

The municipal digitalisation programme is about presence, not feedback: its [first phase covers site and portal infrastructure for communes](2025-09-14-centrifuge-hebdo-digitalisation-communes-cvuc) rather than a dedicated channel, over [335 municipal portals developed and 145 authorities equipped](2026-07-16-antic-urges-north-west-councils-digital-transformation-techafricanews).

Nothing national takes a citizen complaint about a public service and reports what happened to it.

progress: No change, a standing position the base holds for the first time
summary: The local authorities code [requires councils to publish records, budgets, projects and plans on their own electronic site and establishes citizen proposals to communal and regional executives](2019-12-24-loi-2019-024-code-general-ctd-participation-citoyenne).
developments:
Two provisions carry it. [Article 40(3) requires deliberative-body records, budgets, projects, performance reports and development plans to be published on the local authority's own electronic site. Articles 40 and 41, under a section on citizen participation in communal and regional action, establish the mechanism for citizen proposals to communal and regional executives](2019-12-24-loi-2019-024-code-general-ctd-participation-citoyenne). The capture covers 55 of 372 articles.

No compliance figure for the publication duty is published, and against it [48.6 per cent of councils in one region operate functional websites](2026-07-16-antic-urges-north-west-councils-digital-transformation-techafricanews) — so for at least half of them the duty cannot be met.

No count of proposals made under the participation mechanism, and no response to any, is on the record. The national forum that discusses digital policy [issued no resolution or communique](2026-08-25-cameroon-s-igf-2026-bet-on-data-to-connect-public-services-techgriot).

summary: The [2010 statute guarantees access to information and communication technologies at article 32](2010-04-13-loi-2010-002-protection-promotion-personnes-handicapees); an [accessible digital library for 500 print-disabled learners was planned for January 2026](2025-12-22-cbc-health-services-accessible-digital-library).
developments:
The statute is the legal basis: [article 32 covers access to information and communication technologies and article 33 the accessibility of public and private buildings open to the public](2010-04-13-loi-2010-002-protection-promotion-personnes-handicapees). It is implemented by a decree of 26 July 2018 whose text could not be captured, the official page serving only site navigation. Sixteen years on, no accessibility standard, audit or compliance figure under either is held.

2025-12 - a civil-society pilot with two international partners was [planned to launch by January 2026, serving 500 print-disabled learners with converted electronic books and audiobooks, hosted at a regional inclusive education resource centre and grounded in the country's 2021 ratification of the treaty on access to published works](2025-12-22-cbc-health-services-accessible-digital-library). No launch confirmation is held.

The state's own instrument is a card rather than a service: the [national disability card carries income-tax and salary-tax exemption under the 2026 finance law](2026-09-02-cmr-bridging-digital-dividends-safeguarding-disabled-persons-onl).

summary: Two donor registration exercises: [more than 32,600 internally displaced people registered and 2,800 households surveyed in one region](2026-03-17-giz-pesop-idp-profiling-west-region), and a [biometric food-assistance pilot reaching about 4,700 of 5,300 targeted](2026-07-17-un-cameroon-wfp-scope-in-kind-pilot-kolofata).
developments:
2026-03-10 - a profiling project of a German agency and the refugee agency presented results: [more than 32,600 internally displaced people registered and about 2,800 households surveyed across five municipalities in one region, producing an evidence base for municipal service planning and durable-solutions programming](2026-03-17-giz-pesop-idp-profiling-west-region).

2026-07 - a food agency ran the country's first in-kind digital beneficiary pilot in the Far North, [biometrically registering displaced and vulnerable households for food assistance and reaching about 4,700 of a targeted 5,300 beneficiaries with a 98.5 per cent redemption rate, alongside cash assistance reaching 129,500 people nationally](2026-07-17-un-cameroon-wfp-scope-in-kind-pilot-kolofata).

Both are donor systems. Neither is stated to feed the unified social register or the national identity system, and the register itself is [reported at low take-up in the regions where displacement is a named pressure](2026-04-15-cameroon-tribune-resuc-ouest-sensibilises).

summary: The [2021-2030 strategy rests on the 2020 statistics law, whose articles 20 to 22 place it at the centre of statistical activity](2021-01-01-snds30-strategie-nationale-developpement-statistique); a [regional harmonisation project's steering committee first met in February 2026](2026-02-26-cameroon-tribune-hiswaca-comite-pilotage).
developments:
The strategy's copy held [carries no adoption date and the capture reaches its front matter and the opening of the preface only](2021-01-01-snds30-strategie-nationale-developpement-statistique), so its own axes and costings are not on the base. Its legal basis is the [2020 statistics law and the 2021 decree fixing its modalities](2020-07-20-loi-2020-010-activite-statistique-cameroun).

2026-02-25 - the steering committee of a financier-backed regional harmonisation project met for the first time; for this country the project is to [enable migration by 2029 from the enhanced general data dissemination system to the special data dissemination standard, in support of the strategy](2026-02-26-cameroon-tribune-hiswaca-comite-pilotage).

2026-04-07 - the statistical information council's first extraordinary session examined the 2027 annual work plan and recorded that the [2026 plan totalled FCFA 31.5bn, FCFA 12.8bn domestic and FCFA 18.2bn external, funding the sixth household survey, a multiple indicator survey, the population and agriculture censuses and the quarterly employment survey](2026-04-08-cameroon-tribune-cnis-ptba-2027-snis). External financing is the larger share of the programme.

summary: Regional statistical yearbooks are [built from data collected from sectoral administrations, local authorities and enterprises](2026-08-07-ins-annuaire-statistique-adamaoua-2025), under [guidelines the institute issued on statistics from administrative sources](2022-10-14-ins-manuel-lignes-directrices-statistiques-source-administrative).
developments:
The recurring output is what demonstrates administrative data in use rather than in principle: the institute's [regional yearbooks draw on sectoral administrations, decentralised territorial authorities and parapublic and private enterprises, supplemented by national survey data disaggregated to local level](2026-08-07-ins-annuaire-statistique-adamaoua-2025).

The framework above them is the [2020 statistics law with its implementing decree, under which the institute's guidelines on statistics from administrative sources run](2022-10-14-ins-manuel-lignes-directrices-statistiques-source-administrative).

2026-02 - the regional harmonisation project's stakeholder plan [names sectoral administrative-data systems and information systems among the project's components](2026-02-01-ins-hiswaca-pmpp-plan-mobilisation-parties-prenantes).

No count of contributing administrations, no timeliness measure and no completeness rate is published for any of it.

summary: Three externally led uses: a [crop yield mapper adopted in March 2024](2024-03-27-fao-eostat-crop-yield-mapper-capacity-building), [national cocoa and forest land-cover mapping in November 2025](2025-11-25-fao-cocoa-mapping-eu-sustainable-cocoa-programme), and a [peer-reviewed oil-palm quantification in December 2025](2025-12-31-plos-one-sentinel1-oil-palm-cameroon).
developments:
2024-03-26 - a two-day workshop of a food and agriculture agency programme saw the country [adopt an extended crop mapper with a crop-growth model for seasonal crop-distribution mapping and high-resolution yield forecasting, with the agriculture ministry's statistics directorate, the statistics institute, the climate observatory and the agricultural research institute taking part](2024-03-27-fao-eostat-crop-yield-mapper-capacity-building).

2025-11-25 - a workshop presented [national land-cover mapping results using satellite remote sensing, artificial intelligence and cloud tools for cocoa and forest tracking under a European sustainable cocoa programme, supporting deforestation-regulation due diligence, with about 50 participants from government, development partners, civil society and research institutions](2025-11-25-fao-cocoa-mapping-eu-sustainable-cocoa-programme).

2025-12-31 - a peer-reviewed study [used radar imagery and a random forest classifier to quantify oil-palm change from 2015 to 2025, finding increases of 13 to 55 per cent, greatest in the South Region](2025-12-31-plos-one-sentinel1-oil-palm-cameroon).

All three are externally led. No national agricultural earth-observation programme, budget or operational product is held.

summary: The meteorological service has [operational access to a European organisation's nowcasting products](2026-01-20-meteocameroon-nwcsaf-eumetsat) and [hosted a regional forecaster training in Yaounde from 29 June to 3 July 2026](2026-07-08-meteocameroon-crews-swfp-training-yaounde).
developments:
The standing capability is product access: the service has [operational access, through a visualisation platform, to a European satellite organisation's nowcasting products for zero to six hour forecasting](2026-01-20-meteocameroon-nwcsaf-eumetsat).

2026-05 - the country is [one of the planned regional-centre locations for an African meteorological satellite applications facility launched in Addis Ababa under a European-funded early warning project, and was represented by the director of national meteorology and the acting head of the national meteorological centre](2026-05-23-meteocameroon-sewa-amsaf-launch-addis-abeba).

2026-07 - it hosted a [regional training for 23 forecasters from the regional centre, the central African climate centre and the air navigation agency, covering satellite-based nowcasting products](2026-07-08-meteocameroon-crews-swfp-training-yaounde) — the second such training hosted in two years, tied to the service's ambition to become a regional specialised meteorological centre.

The one national use of satellite data outside meteorology is enumeration: [smartphone enumeration combined with satellite imagery and sample estimation, adopted for areas inaccessible through insecurity or isolation](2026-03-11-leconomie-census-2026-digital-satellite-data-collection).

summary: An exploration and no instrument: the finance minister [received a Dubai-based financial group on 7 January 2026 to explore financing for projects including digital infrastructure](2026-01-07-minfi-sgc-financement-projets-structurants).
developments:
2026-01-07 - the meeting explored a [structured financing line for strategic projects in energy, housing and digital infrastructure under the national development strategy](2026-01-07-minfi-sgc-financement-projets-structurants). No amount, instrument or signature is stated, and it is a distinct meeting from a separate ministerial audience with the same counterpart nine days later.

That is the whole of the Gulf engagement the base holds. No technology investment, data-centre commitment or digital memorandum with any Gulf state is on the record, and the one large private data-centre commitment in the country is [American rather than Gulf](2026-09-07-cmr-businessincameroon-cybastion-75m).
